Black Squad doesn't seem all that original compared to other shooters, but I'm not sure it was trying to be. Certainly it isn't going after new-to-the-genre players, as the tutorial/training modes could only be called inadequate for actual training.
There are both quick-respawn deathmatch and team-based objective missions, but most players gravitate to deathmatch for quick play so they don't have to spend most of the time spectating. The added classes of Destruction mode may indeed be the deepest aspect of the game, but they are hard to experiment with since they aren't available in training and can't be switched mid-match. This is something I hope NS Studio adds to practice mode (at minimum), because I think it might hook people if it wasn't so inscrutable.
Overall if you really like PvP shooters and want to try a different take, you'll find Black Squad competent and even prefer it to competitors. But if you're looking for something that innovates on the traditional shooter, I can't say this is it. It's exactly as fun as other games in the FPS genre; no worse, no better.

XCOM 2 is a solid game. Just like the first XCOM reboot.
That being said, XCOM 2 almost feels more like an expansion to the first game than another game itself. There's a few changes to the core gameplay, but most of the original themes are unchanged. In a sense, XCOM 2 feels like a reboot of XCOM without a the graphical overhaul that usually comes with a reboot.
If you enjoyed the last XCOM then you'll enjoy this XCOM. It didn't take very many chances, and where it did it stumbled a bit. The stealth mechanic you sometimes get at the beginning of missions encourages more tactical setups before a fight, which is nice, but since most of the missions have a turn limit you feel more rushed than before. This is both good and bad. It means your success relies even more on tactical play than in the previous game, but it also makes the game a little more stressful. Some changes were odd; for instance, psionic characters have to train in their base instead of leveling up in the field to get new abilities. This undermines one of the game's core mechanics and makes for inconsistant gameplay. For example, it's disappointing when your psionic character gets a kill because it means that they won't get a promotion for it. It should always feel rewarding for a character to get a kill.
A few of the changes were positive. The new overworld map with a mobile base allowed for far more interesting non-combat gameplay. The loss of willpower soldiers get after traumatic encounters puts a bit more attrition in your army so you can't as easily rely on a single powerful strike team. The increased health and explosive potential of your troops later in the game allows you to have ever grander skirmishes than before.
Should you buy this game? If you want more XCOM, this will give you more XCOM. If you're satisfied with what the last game gave you, though, there's not a lot to be found here. If you like turn based strategy games, then this will keep you entertained. Personally, I recommend waiting for a Steam sale and getting it on discount unless you're loyal to the franchise.

This game is hard, brutal, and unforgiving - AND I LOVE IT! More-so then even other intense games like XCOM. Deaths are almost a guarantee if you do everything right - despite all my efforts, several of my 5th and 6th level heroes kicked the bucket near the end. But that's the point - as the narrator says "darkness, but beyond, the glint of gold..." is what keeps you going and pushing deeper into the depths.
Darkest Dungeon is a story about coping with loss. The loss of characters can be unfortunate, and extremely frustrating at times. You can try to skirt that, but some death is inevitable, like in the real world. Leveling your characters up and watching them grow is part of the fun, but I think many people don't understand or appreciate that the real progression mechanic of the game is the artifacts and upgrade system of the game. As long as you don't lose your whole party, you can limp back with your precious artifacts.
On that topic, a lot of people seem to have trouble with the item management subgame - I just treat it like a real week-long expedition (lots of torches and food until you have your feet under you, couple shovels/keys). Consumable exploratory items are often what can determine whether a character lives or survive, or more importantly if you get that hefty payout to allow you keep strengthening your characters equipment. Which again, I consider a perk in its favor. If you run out of money, then things get harder, obviously.
I enjoy the fact that economics are more important then people's lives for this one, ultimately - that your gold is on the level of being as important as your hero's strength. I find the cost saving upgrades, especially for the sanitarium, to be incredible investments, unlike most games where it's merely superflous. It's a lot of fun culling the bad traits and strengthening the good ones when you can. This is no place for the weak of resolve, or the weak of heart - better to just cut them loose. But that's part of the fun!
Trying to keep your characters sane is a fun, tense mechanic. Most of the time they crack in the worst ways, but sometimes its the best of ways, and that unexpected victory in the face of expected defeat, triumphing over the worst odds rarely is what makes the game come alive. I might suggest its even the theme of the game, to be perfectly honest. The Lovecraftian style is absolutely amazing - one of the more unhinging, disturbingly beautiful aspects I've seen in years.
Perfectionists may want to consider looking elsewhere unless the RNG smiles on you, and powergamers will need to accept some level of loss and frustration. Hence the poor game reviews from people who can't handle their favorite heroes dying, or who lost their artifacts trying to finish when they should have run away. I find their hatred and tears on the reviews (yes, even this one) amusing since it misses the point.
To enjoy it more, from my experience just be smart, cut your losses and minimize risks to your truly valuable resources. If you start viewing it like a real dungeon exploration manager would; suddenly this game becomes a lot more fun. You can get salty when your favorite character dies, but there's no need to let that salt ruin the stew.
One last, NG+ is hard as♥♥♥♥♥♥from what I've read, even compared to the base game. Still in the final stages of working through it. But that's amazing in my book.
EDIT:  Just for reference, there's a posse of about 10-20 people who just troll around downvoting all positive reviews or anyone who has a nice thing to say about it. Just ignore the trolls and basically the whole "helpfulness" metric of reviews when it comes to this game.

I'm not too sure where to begin so I'll just weigh up both the pros and cons of the game,
I also come from having never played a previous Souls game so I'm talking about DS3 exclusive to bias from nostalgia
Pros;
Smooth combat,
Great personalization,
Gorgeous graphics,
Fluid level design,
Varied enemies,
Medievil post-apocalyptic aesthetic (A pro if you're into that kinda stuff),
Epic and memorable boss fights,
A lot more that you'll just have to find for yourself,
Co-op gameplay while retaining the single player game feeling
The soundtrack.
Cons;
The Pvp,
Lack of replayability,
Unbalanced,
Requires a lot of the player, (Which can be either a good or bad thing depending on whom is playing)
In-Bloody-vasions,
The conniptions that it will give you.
Right, so a lot of that needs further explaination so here we go chaps:
The game feels great to play, it looks absolutely fantastic, the boss fights feel immersive, epic and keep you on your toes. The game is unforgiving but feels just about fair. Nothing feels unbeatable (Except Midir, he needs to end himself). The combat never feels clunky and because of the great visual effects and sound design everything feels real, like the swords feel like they have weight to them that makes sense. You can choose exactly how you play and your character is truly yours due to not having generic skill tree paths.
However getting into the game is very difficult and requires the player to really want to like dark souls. Unless you're some kind of demi-god (Or have prior Souls experience) the first boss will keep you stuck for a while but it teaches you a lot about how the game is structured overall. The game does a very good job or not explaining anything to you and a lot of the fun is exploring how stuff works for the first time, past your first playthrough the game starts to feel repetative and you need to do challenge runs to keep things fun really. I'm also quite happy they didn't add a difficulty setting but instead added a more challenging version of the game once you complete the game once, which ramps up everytime you beat the game up until New Game +9, unfortunately they did my least favourite thing that games do with difficulty settings which is just sticking the health and damage of enemies on a multiplier and letting the game become unfair instead of giving you more or a challenge to overcome. I'd much rather they make the AI more intelligent and perhaps make new enemies or versions of the current enemies that compensate for the weaknesses the normal enemy has.
The biggest downpoint for me is the PvP: The connectivity is total trash, parry is pure luck and everyone feels like butter where all you have to do is mash RB a bunch until you out poise the enemy and make them waste all of their estai. (Healing item) The invasion system is the worst thing I've ever seen honestly. Other players can enter matchmaking and it will put them in a random world as a red phantom (A ghost of another player that can't interact with the world, only attack you and any of your summoned phantoms) A red phantom can only invade you if you're embered though (A power up that increases your total health 30%, allows you to summon phantoms to aid you but allows red phantoms to invade you) you recieve a free ember after killing any boss but this feels like a hinderance. When a red phantom invades you usually it will just waste everyone's time. The red phantom usually won't stand a chance because he'll be up against three players and you can't really fight three players at once unless you're really skilled and lucky. Or the red phantom will be up against 1 player who will have double their estus flasks, so you'll both just RB each other until you've lost half your estai and a lot of time where they'll then just run away to hide behind enemies that can't attack them so you can't move up because they'll then gank you so you sit and wait for a very long time, and honestly the whole thing makes co-op a horrible experience and getting the ember after a boss fight like punmishment.
That was a bit of a personal rant and I still love the game overall but you've got to know what you're in for.
To summarize: the game is very much like a groundhogs day of your journey and feels like bashing your head against your wall for a lot of time. If you hate yourself then this game is perfect for you, enjoy kiddos

Hey fellow gamers!
So this is my first time taking the time to write a review:
The main takaway from this is, if you liked XCOM 1, buy this game. It's much more cinematic, customizable, and expansive. It retains the personal feelings you develop with each of your operatives as well as the devastating feeling of losing them in combat. It's fun and definitely did not take a step backwards in regards to fun and replayability. I'm beginning the "Commander's" campaign now.
Negatives (Opinion):
-A lot of missions are now on a timer, which forces you to take one approach. Rush forward. It's fun at first, but it should've been limited to just a few missions, not the majority.
-You no longer have the ability to capture live speciments. Some people like this, some don't. I enjoyed the rewarding feeling of locking up a live Berserker in containment. It made you feel powerful.
-There are no more Mech's.
-Your operatives will almost always die, rather than start "bleeding out" It only happened to me once during the entire campaign and that was with one of my Colonel's.
-"Will" doesn't really seem to make any difference. I had one operative that had his will stat maxxed out, and he would still panic all the time.
-FINALLY: Injuries. It doesn't matter if your operative only takes 2 blocks of damage, they will almost ALWAYS return from the fight "Critically Injured" with a one month recovery period. It's annoying.

this game wants to be so fun, i really want to like this game, but everytime i play im disappointed.
i think my main issue is the RNG which is terrible...you could set up a perfect ambush and your entire squad will miss. or your CQB guy with a shotgun will miss a 10ft tall target within arms reach of himself. things like that. This game requires no skill, because in the end its coming down to some dice rolls which i believe to be statistically fake. what do i mean by that? i mean that your chance to hit is pre determined before you click fire. you can hit against 5% odds and reload the game and hit 5% again and again. the roll isnt made when click the fire button, which is when it should be.
the AI is kinda screwy, some of them will suicide rush through 4 squad members and crossfire to get to one person in the back,and because of either misses or HP pool they will usually heavily damge,stun or kill them, and theres not much you can do to prevent it other than set the entire squad to overwatch and hope he gets cliped out before he wales on someone.
sometimes you will lose a squad member through no fault of your own. they could be in 100% cover and get crited from full hp and just die. yep the guy who youve been grooming for 11 missions gets one shots and you literally could not have put him in better cover.
another one of my favorites is the poisonous spiders, which IMO are broken. basically,you get no warning of their arrival, they just show up. they pop out of the ground suicide rush you and poisen you with a possibility of one shotting you on your turn.
example. i see one go underground behind a house, i think to myself "haha i have you now" so i place a squad member to the corner of the house so when the spider pops out ,he can get a shot in. what actually happens is i place the guy at the corner of the house ,the game stops his turn before i can put him on overwatch. spider pops out of the ground ,runs over takes 90% of his hp. then goes back to my guy again...who then proceeds to miss the pointblank shot,and dies from poisen. literally the exact thing i moved him to to prevent happened. wouldnt it make more sense to move the guy to corner , to watch for the spider you know is going to come out,then when he does-shoot him? rather than move to corner and wait for him to comeover and kill you?
i think the way reactions are done is a bit screwed as well.
- if you get spotted by the aliens on your turn, they get a reaction move ,then their normal turn.
- if you get spotted by the aliens on their turn, they get a reaction move.

as far as im concearned you should be afforded the same reaction move they get. so that way you can at least defend yourself instead of watching them run across the map.

XCOM 2 is a solid game. Just like the first XCOM reboot.
That being said, XCOM 2 almost feels more like an expansion to the first game than another game itself. There's a few changes to the core gameplay, but most of the original themes are unchanged. In a sense, XCOM 2 feels like a reboot of XCOM without a the graphical overhaul that usually comes with a reboot.
If you enjoyed the last XCOM then you'll enjoy this XCOM. It didn't take very many chances, and where it did it stumbled a bit. The stealth mechanic you sometimes get at the beginning of missions encourages more tactical setups before a fight, which is nice, but since most of the missions have a turn limit you feel more rushed than before. This is both good and bad. It means your success relies even more on tactical play than in the previous game, but it also makes the game a little more stressful. Some changes were odd; for instance, psionic characters have to train in their base instead of leveling up in the field to get new abilities. This undermines one of the game's core mechanics and makes for inconsistant gameplay. For example, it's disappointing when your psionic character gets a kill because it means that they won't get a promotion for it. It should always feel rewarding for a character to get a kill.
A few of the changes were positive. The new overworld map with a mobile base allowed for far more interesting non-combat gameplay. The loss of willpower soldiers get after traumatic encounters puts a bit more attrition in your army so you can't as easily rely on a single powerful strike team. The increased health and explosive potential of your troops later in the game allows you to have ever grander skirmishes than before.
Should you buy this game? If you want more XCOM, this will give you more XCOM. If you're satisfied with what the last game gave you, though, there's not a lot to be found here. If you like turn based strategy games, then this will keep you entertained. Personally, I recommend waiting for a Steam sale and getting it on discount unless you're loyal to the franchise.

Well this game is really fun so far. I'm not even that far into it but I'm definitely happy with getting the game on sale.
There's a lot I really like in this game. From the Lovecraftian themes to the ideals of depression showen in the game as it uses stress as a game function. The stress function is adds a bit of randomness to the game, which makes it so that you'll consider using things that lower your stress so that you don't get negative effects that change specific stats, as your character becomes more and more insane due to a heightened stress level they do various things. Character afflicted with the irrational trait will use moves without player input and characters who have become masochistic will jump at any chance to open something that might have a trap or hurt themselves instead of doing a player input action. Though raising the stress to 100 (out of a maximum of 200) could also give them a buff if they become inspired, ferocious, or courageous. It's a bit of a gamble when you do get to that point to see if you'll get a massive debuff and negative affects, or you'll get a massive buff and positive affects.
The game even allows you to cheat death by having a "Death's Door" effect, where every attack from an enemy has a chance of killing that character. I've used this function to get out of dungeons with all of my characters alive, though in major need ot stress relief.
The premise of this game is that you basically form a mercenary company.
If you like the writings of H.P. Lovecraft then you'll probably like this game, the same goes for if you like gothic psychological horror games.
So far it's a 7/10 for me.

Compared to XCOM EU and EW, XCOM2 doesn't live up to its expectations. The overall feeling I got from the game was 'weird' and the story isn't much better either (What the F happened to Bradford?!) The missions lack variety after a while and the timers are not neccesarily a welcome addition, except for the hard core players. But where xcom:eu delivered a far better, somewhat arcade-ish experience, Xcom 2 is focussed much more at the tactical layer at the cost of the overall game experience. There is for example no real base manegement and the UFO hunts have been eliminated from the game. The random maps make it impossible for the A.I. to set you up for a trap when exploring rooms. In Xcom:EU you had to search rooms and buildings and behind every door was the fear of an ambush lurking. That is completely gone now.
The commander difficulty was rewarding but I felt the game was cut short with the final mission. The "Legendary" difficulty setting is a joke. The AI cheats on you and percentages are off. The procedurally generated missions are boring, short and dull and I'll take XCOM:EU maps over any procedurally created map any day.
Visually it is a game but again it lacks the enticement here. There are for example no fancy cutscenes when assaulting mutons barehanded that felt so rewarding when watching. Also the somewhat comical tone of XCom:EU is gone and the dev crew tried to make the game look more natural. In which they have succeed but again, at the cost of something good. The slight comical tone of XCom:EU added more drama to the story.
In general, I feel XCOM 2 was rushed and released to appease only the modding community. It feels like a present to the modding community to thank them for extending XCOM:EU with the LW mod. I also highly doubt if the dev's are really satisfied with the result themselves. Imo, theres a line in how much you listen to your fanbase and change the course of their own vision of how their game should be. In this case, that line has been crossed and the result is a 'game' that's barely worth calling a game, considering how fast you can finish it.
Fans of XCOM should however buy this game because there's nothing else right now to quench your thirst for TBS gaming and maybe my review is a bit harsh but I was really looking forward to the sequel of one of my all time favorite games. Guess I just overhyped myself.

Being a player of both space RPG's (EVE and STO) and FPS's (Battlefield and CoD) I must say that for an alpha, this looks like it could go somewhere. I feel like the are going for a Dota or LoL style lane fighting, but without Ai units or shops. Instead the lanes have capture zones, and all pushing is done by playes.
Pros-
-Great graphics if you have the rig to handle it.
-Teamwork is key, some may say its a con but in my book its great.
-The fights are great when its more than just a 1v1 encounter
-I loved the feel of flying a massive space tank.
Cons-
-Ship balancing needs to happen, but this is expected as it is still in alpha.
-I feel like they are pushing MMOBA type lanes that really dont work without AI ships of some sort.
-Battles can be very one sided if one or two players on the other team know what they are doing, some sort of ranked matchmaking really should be implemented. However again, its alpha, so this could still be coming,
Conclusion-
I have played for only a few hours but I can say I plan on continuing to play. I really liked the almost FPS feel to massive ship battles, its a fun change from the click and roll face across the keyboard I am used to. Fact is that I am usually very critical of any kind of space ship shoot em up games, but even in alpha this is one that I am enjoying a lot. I recommend this to people who have some patients, as it does have a learning curve.

Timed missions, poor UI, icon clearing.  Tis just not fun unless your on the ground!
It's not a bad game but I'm really struggling to want to play anything other than the ground missions.
The ground missions are great (well, apart from doing timed missions constantly) and aspects of it have been improved from the first game.  The new alien designs seem quite cool and the random maps are great as well.  There were a few parts of the game I enjoy until.....
- I am not in a ground mission.  They've put in a lot more complexity in the base/map part of the game but I find it confusing and uninteresting on the whole.
- The ground mission is another timed mission.  I cans ee why they have done it and it does add a bit more bite to the missions.  Save scumming is the new overwatch now!
- I had to use a mouse and keyboard as there is no controller support (Steampad doesn't count!).  You can play it well enough with the mouse and keyboard on the ground missions but the UI for the base/map section is difficult to navigate with them.  It looks like it would be easier to navigate with a controller but you can't use one!
- Easy is very easy, normal is very difficult.  I have played old X-Com and new X-Com and found the recommended difficulty far too hard at times.  When I changed it down to easy the aliens were suddenly made out of butter and it wasn't a challenge.
- I had to listen to the voice acting far too often.  Some of it is ok, all of it grates eventually because you can't do anything in this game without someone having something to say about it.
- I had to look at my rag tag bunch of misfits standing with "attitude".  I'm not big into customisation but even I was tempted to use it when I saw the poor models you get as standard.  I'm also not a fan of the posing (but I understand this is more personal preference on my part.)
- I had to sit through the beginning and end animations again.  You do quite a few ground missions and I got fed up of the animations that I had to 'Esc' through constantly to get past them.
It's just not my cup of tea to be honest.  The choices they've made have taken a lot of the fun out of it for me and on top of that they have made some decisions that I just don't understand (like taking controller support out of a game which had previously amazed everyone with how well it worked with a controller.)  Shame as I was looking forward to this!
EDITTED TO ADD (as I've now finished it, no spoilers)
- The ground game really is good fun.  If I didn't dislike the other stuff so much it might have been a recommend (and while it's great, it's not that much of a change from the first one.  It's tweaked very well though.)
- The story is a bit tonally strange (can't decide if it wants to be a serious game or not) and didn't really like any of the characters.  It's also a bit light until the end.
- Can't really say too much about the end  as I don't won't to spoil it but....
The final mission is jarring as characters appear that you have either not seen, or barely seen throughout the game so far.  The end is a bit of an anti climax (X-Com 1 has a better ending!)

Where else can you invade another player and spend 30 minutes trying to find them, and when you finally do, you're both so impressed by each other's respective hiding and seeking skills that instead of fighting, you dance around each other, chug all your estus, and commit mutual ritualistic suicide with clouds of deadly mercury? Dark souls 3 is one of the best horror-action RPGs of all time, but the multiplayer is one of the best comedy games of all time. Nothing else (aside from sometimes other souls games) comes close to this kind of wild and fleeting anonymous multiplayer magic. It's also incredibly beautifully art-directed, the music is pretty good, the sound design is incredible and satisfying, the feel of controlling the character is near perfect in how weighty but responsive it is, the story is fascinating in how it takes the existing lore of dark souls and twists it and recontextualizes it, and the RPG systems are really fun to figure out and all feed back into the gameplay in cool ways. It also has some great level design and by far the best boss fights in the history of video game. I will never forget finally beating Darkeater Midir or Sister Friede after hours of gradually mastering every movement and reaction and attack. Very few games can inspire awe, joy, triumph, fear, and hilarious laughing fits, but this one does all of that. Absolute Game of the Century.

Well this game is really fun so far. I'm not even that far into it but I'm definitely happy with getting the game on sale.
There's a lot I really like in this game. From the Lovecraftian themes to the ideals of depression showen in the game as it uses stress as a game function. The stress function is adds a bit of randomness to the game, which makes it so that you'll consider using things that lower your stress so that you don't get negative effects that change specific stats, as your character becomes more and more insane due to a heightened stress level they do various things. Character afflicted with the irrational trait will use moves without player input and characters who have become masochistic will jump at any chance to open something that might have a trap or hurt themselves instead of doing a player input action. Though raising the stress to 100 (out of a maximum of 200) could also give them a buff if they become inspired, ferocious, or courageous. It's a bit of a gamble when you do get to that point to see if you'll get a massive debuff and negative affects, or you'll get a massive buff and positive affects.
The game even allows you to cheat death by having a "Death's Door" effect, where every attack from an enemy has a chance of killing that character. I've used this function to get out of dungeons with all of my characters alive, though in major need ot stress relief.
The premise of this game is that you basically form a mercenary company.
If you like the writings of H.P. Lovecraft then you'll probably like this game, the same goes for if you like gothic psychological horror games.
So far it's a 7/10 for me.

First off I`d like to start with only get this game if you have played through and completed XCOM: Enemy Unknown and its dlc, Enemy Within.
The first impressions I had of this game was it isn't easy. It's quite hard and downright vicious on the later difficulties. Commander is a "fun challenge" , while Legend is downright brutal and will punish you if you make a single mistake, especially enjoyable if you're doing ironman or enjoy pain.                                                                                                                                                                                      The second impression that struck me is that it plays a lot like XCOM: Enemy Unknown/ Within yet it has new mechanics to spice up the game play. One of the newest and my personal favorite additions is squad concealment, a mechanic that allows you to make a jump on a enemy pod or have the enemy pod jump you.
A feature that was in Enemy Unknown was customizations , but unlike the last game you can customize about anything on a character: tattoos, facial hair, biographies, hats, even weapons. The new aliens and ADVENT troops are another thing that I absolutely love. Each different troop has a different potential to wreak havoc upon your unlucky solders and it make you prioritize them depending on the situation. A troop may be ignored as harmless given what else is in play but can also be the biggest threat another time. The aliens themselves are well designed and generally balanced(Unless you consider some of the new abilities gained as unfair).
As for the graphic design of the maps I have to say the devs did a stunning job. The randomly generated maps that are made for each mission to ensure no 2 missions have the same map is another wonderful touch. As for the story goes its well planned but contains several open ends as to why things play out as they do. As far as the "ant farm" on the Avenger is concerned it is the same with a few tweaks to building items and weapon/armor tier upgrades. Research is the same as Enemy Unknown but completely different from those of the last game.
The new classes are fun with all of the new combos and builds you can set up(i.e.; a ranger suited for scouting or being up close and personal). The combat itself is once again fun as it being XCOM you never know if a 1% shot will hit or a 99% shot will miss( both have happened , the missing the 99% more often ).                                                                                                                                                               	One of the largest things I`ve come to love is the modding support. I'm not going to lie when I say having a corgi gun to a Bob Ross  voice pack to having even more aliens and other little customizations of options added is one of the best things to happen. Being able to expand a game once all dlc is out will help draw out even more hours to the game play as you can combine and try different modded play-through.
With the recent patch out having fixed most if not all game breaking bugs and glitches,  making changes to video settings and optimatizations, and of course several small nerfs (mimic beacon). That and a  dlc relapsing on March 17 with several hundred more solider and weapon customizations is truly impressive.

Solid 9.3/10 because several smaller bugs are still present but overall doesn't take too much attention away from the engaging strategic game play.

Is this a point and click game where you randomly fire at anyone in range? yeah it is. BUT! there is a kinda team fortress 2 type of teamwork involved too which is where the game really shines.
Fractured Space follows a rock paper scissors type of set up with its ships. For example, a Flagship has a lot of health and can take a pretty serious beating but its slow and its firepower is about average for the ships in game. A brawler has a massive amount of damage but its equivalent to a shotgun where all the damage only occurs at near point blank range. A sniper can do a massive amount of damage with its upgrade but its all but a glass cannon with very little health. A hunter has a moderate amount of firepower with average health but it has the special ability to make short range jumps allowing it to quickly close larges distances.
So a brawler can rip apart a flagship, a sniper can rip apart a brawler, a hunter can close in quickly and rip apart a sniper and a flagship can rip apart a hunter. Rock, paper, scissors.
It doesnt sound terribly interesting but the maps are fairly well done allowing for strategy and in pubs it requires real teamwork to achieve the larger goal of capturing the enemy base. PLUS! there is as yet no pay to win.
The game is neat, not revolutionary by anymeans but a a good time killer. And as of this writing its free, so meh why turn down a free game :P

This game is, and this hurts to say as a fan of Fallout since the first game by interplay, really bad.
- The optimization is awful and it runs poorly even on fairly powerful machines. That's because shadows and many clutter textures are at 4k resolution SIZE without actually being 4k in detail, essentially bad textures taking up as much space on your graphic RAM as high-definition ones.
- Weapon modification means while the guns you have can be enhanced and changed to fit new roles, there's barely any variety and many weapons have been  cut completely from the game, because the ones you have technically could fill the role of these weapons but they're just not as good. No 10mm SMG, no 14mm guns, one sniper rifle, one assault rifle... just overall less variety.
- Bugs. Many game-breaking or quest-ending bugs are still in the game years after the initial release. These had to have been fixed by modders because the official developer and publisher of the game is not interested in fixing them, it seems. This has been an issue with Bethesda games pretty much forever and I understand that the size and complexity of the game means that some bugs simply will remain. However, known, well-documented and game-breaking bugs still remaining in the game after years of patching are just inexcusable.
- Quests are boring. This is one of my main complaints about a game that is trying to market itself as an RPG. You should be invested in the world but you just aren't. The dialogue system is a joke, usually giving you four variations of the same answer. You can be snarky, helpful or apprehensive but do it anyway or say no and do it later, is what it boils down to. This is not an RPG. You cannot roleplay a character in any way safe the "I will do everything for everyone" approach or the raging cannibal who kills everyone. There's no shades of grey, no moral ambiguity. Something that has been a problem in Bethesda games before, morality is purely binary.
I have never managed to get anywhere near the end in the main quest because I simply do not care. I saw the twist coming basically from the moment I left the initial vault and I felt very railroaded (no pun intended) in how I could approach it. Sidequests are usually not very interesting either and the Radiant Quests are literally busywork with interchangeable objectives that boil down to "Find X while fighting through location Y" or "kill all X in location Y", repeated ad nauseam.
- Combat. If the quests in this Action/RPG are boring, surely they made a fun combat system to compensate? No. Combat is barebones and usually just a matter of turning on VATS. Cover doesn't exist as such, as even a wooden pallet or a thin, rusty section of sheet metal will block a bullet. The player can shoot through some of these with a perk upgrade, but it's usually easier to just run around and gun the enemy down. And of course there's the old problem of "Is someone there? Must have been my imagination" of enemies that just saw their friend explode in a shower of gore but you passed your stealth check. They then continue to be alerted as gunshots and explosions rattle the building and a power-armored maniac is killing everyone, but their pathfinding AI didn't manage to find them a path to it so they just all cluster in front of a door, waiting for you to show up.
- Settlement building. This feature was NOT made for mouse and keyboard or ease of access. Every menu screams controller optimisation. Despite hundreds of objects being available, you have to scroll through the menus and submenus item by item and look for what you were trying to find. No lists, no search function, no tags. It also takes a long time to load objects without an SSD. Placing objects is a nightmare on many parts, finding the one piece where a rooftop wants to connect to the rooftops around it without spinning into a new direction or turning upside down is incredibly frustrating.
I have the utmost respect for anyone creating impressive fortresses and detailed builds with this broken system, but I just don't bother anymore. Settlement defense is a 51/49% chance anyhow, no matter how many walls and turrets you place down, enemies will spawn inside the build area anyway if you come to defend it, and the settlers don't even need to be able to access their beds. You could literally build a massive concrete tower with no way to access it and place everything on top of it and it would still be raided successfully half the time by 5 raiders using poorly-maintained guns.
-Mods... Now all of these issues can and have been addressed by mods, but then Bethesda decided to first try paid mods. They failed horribly. Now they're using the Creation Club and apparently have learned nothing but also made a system that is even worse given how it impacts performance of the game. The Creation Club files are downloaded automatically whether you want the mod or not, take up huge amounts of space due to being poorly compressed and every new upgrade changes the .EXE files of the other mods, thus requiring F4SE to be updated. This company has continuosly impressed me by how utterly incompetent they appear.
Unless something actually changes in Bethesda's policies, this was the last game I bought from this company.

Well this game is really fun so far. I'm not even that far into it but I'm definitely happy with getting the game on sale.
There's a lot I really like in this game. From the Lovecraftian themes to the ideals of depression showen in the game as it uses stress as a game function. The stress function is adds a bit of randomness to the game, which makes it so that you'll consider using things that lower your stress so that you don't get negative effects that change specific stats, as your character becomes more and more insane due to a heightened stress level they do various things. Character afflicted with the irrational trait will use moves without player input and characters who have become masochistic will jump at any chance to open something that might have a trap or hurt themselves instead of doing a player input action. Though raising the stress to 100 (out of a maximum of 200) could also give them a buff if they become inspired, ferocious, or courageous. It's a bit of a gamble when you do get to that point to see if you'll get a massive debuff and negative affects, or you'll get a massive buff and positive affects.
The game even allows you to cheat death by having a "Death's Door" effect, where every attack from an enemy has a chance of killing that character. I've used this function to get out of dungeons with all of my characters alive, though in major need ot stress relief.
The premise of this game is that you basically form a mercenary company.
If you like the writings of H.P. Lovecraft then you'll probably like this game, the same goes for if you like gothic psychological horror games.
So far it's a 7/10 for me.

A good twist on the MOBA genre, just with more spaceships, guns, lasers and missiles! Which is good, at least if you are a Sci-FI fan.
The game is also deeper than it looks, requiring a hefty amount teamwork (although its very possible to carry, especially at lower levels), with differentiated ships that feel and play significantly different. Whether you enjoy being right in the middle of the fray, a sneaky skirmisher or even a support role (i.e. healer/babysitter), there's always an option for you.
Personally I enjoyed the CTF / Dominion style of map, with multiple segregated zones. The ability to warp to bases makes the game a lot more fluid - there's always action at some point in the map, yet the hefty cooldown attached to it means you must make strategic choices. Warping to the wrong station at the wrong time will mean your allies will lose your support for a good 30 seconds or so. "But I'm split pushing!". Yeah right.
Battles are slower paced, and streamlined. Fights are all carried out in 3D, and your ship has a maingun tied to the mouse, it is as easy as aiming at the enemy and just holding down left click. Missiles attached to 1, drones 2, and so on. Yet, spaceships are not as mobile as let's say, a humanoid hero. Turning, accelerating, even aiming the guns take a decent amount of time. Get caught in a wrong spot, and the enemy ships will fry you in a couple of seconds, but blindside them, and even a frigate can make lightwork of an enemy flagship. This game rewards positioning in spades, and the feeling of outwitting the opponent is extremely satisfying.
If you are a fan of MOBA genres, or even Star Wars Battlefront II (the one with Xwings and TIE fighters), I strongly suggest to give this game a try.
Pros:
-Lasers, Missiles, and Railguns
-No farming, last hitting
-Relatively Lag Proof, due to the positional focused nature of battles
Cons:
-Have to spend time to unlock your ships and weapons.

Where to even begin. The Xcom series has always stolen my heart and Xcom 2 is no exception. After spending just under 61 hours into the game and finally beating it i'm only left with the feeling of accomplishment. The introduction to the game was well put together and created a perfect enviornment to get into. Xcom 2 is fun on all difficulty levels, which still provides a level of challenge and butt-clenching moments.
I'd like to start with a awesome expirence I got to go through.(No Spoilers)
My squad of 6 fully teired soldiers including the 7th unit you gain later on into the game were surrounded on all sides. My gun slinger "Flatline" has just lived through four attacks leaving him down to 4 health. His stasis vest had already run out of charges and he was flanked from all sides with no where to go. My Marksman "the kid" sat behind a burning pillar suppressed by a standard muton. With a 8% chance of hitting a enemy which was flanking flatline actually hit it's target and put an end to the foe. One of my heavy's "volcano" had been knocked unconsious by an enemy earlier in the fight. "Lynx" my combat medic ran through fire,poison,acid, (not kidding) smoke, and a hail of gunfire to not only bring my heavy to a safe location, but also brought him back into the fight. The rest of the squad held their ground exchanging attacks back and forth. One turn on the clock until the mission would be finally over. By this point They had already killed 39 foes and were still engaging another 14. All it took to end the mission was killing one specific enemy. The problem was that the majority of my team had already spent their turns or were suppressed. Until luck threw me a bone. By some miracle my ranger, "Judgment Day" Ran a hail marry over half the battlefield and made the winning slice. All the  time spent on that campaign, the countless losses we endured weren't in vein. The war had been won.
This review will not go into depth about the mechanics or anything in detail, but rather tell a story and pretty much leave it at that.
Lastly I'd like to talk about the game as a whole.
-Is Xcom 2 perfect?
A: Never will be perfect.
-Is Xcom 2 buggy?

First off I`d like to start with only get this game if you have played through and completed XCOM: Enemy Unknown and its dlc, Enemy Within.
The first impressions I had of this game was it isn't easy. It's quite hard and downright vicious on the later difficulties. Commander is a "fun challenge" , while Legend is downright brutal and will punish you if you make a single mistake, especially enjoyable if you're doing ironman or enjoy pain.                                                                                                                                                                                      The second impression that struck me is that it plays a lot like XCOM: Enemy Unknown/ Within yet it has new mechanics to spice up the game play. One of the newest and my personal favorite additions is squad concealment, a mechanic that allows you to make a jump on a enemy pod or have the enemy pod jump you.
A feature that was in Enemy Unknown was customizations , but unlike the last game you can customize about anything on a character: tattoos, facial hair, biographies, hats, even weapons. The new aliens and ADVENT troops are another thing that I absolutely love. Each different troop has a different potential to wreak havoc upon your unlucky solders and it make you prioritize them depending on the situation. A troop may be ignored as harmless given what else is in play but can also be the biggest threat another time. The aliens themselves are well designed and generally balanced(Unless you consider some of the new abilities gained as unfair).
As for the graphic design of the maps I have to say the devs did a stunning job. The randomly generated maps that are made for each mission to ensure no 2 missions have the same map is another wonderful touch. As for the story goes its well planned but contains several open ends as to why things play out as they do. As far as the "ant farm" on the Avenger is concerned it is the same with a few tweaks to building items and weapon/armor tier upgrades. Research is the same as Enemy Unknown but completely different from those of the last game.
The new classes are fun with all of the new combos and builds you can set up(i.e.; a ranger suited for scouting or being up close and personal). The combat itself is once again fun as it being XCOM you never know if a 1% shot will hit or a 99% shot will miss( both have happened , the missing the 99% more often ).                                                                                                                                                               	One of the largest things I`ve come to love is the modding support. I'm not going to lie when I say having a corgi gun to a Bob Ross  voice pack to having even more aliens and other little customizations of options added is one of the best things to happen. Being able to expand a game once all dlc is out will help draw out even more hours to the game play as you can combine and try different modded play-through.
With the recent patch out having fixed most if not all game breaking bugs and glitches,  making changes to video settings and optimatizations, and of course several small nerfs (mimic beacon). That and a  dlc relapsing on March 17 with several hundred more solider and weapon customizations is truly impressive.

Solid 9.3/10 because several smaller bugs are still present but overall doesn't take too much attention away from the engaging strategic game play.

Well this game is really fun so far. I'm not even that far into it but I'm definitely happy with getting the game on sale.
There's a lot I really like in this game. From the Lovecraftian themes to the ideals of depression showen in the game as it uses stress as a game function. The stress function is adds a bit of randomness to the game, which makes it so that you'll consider using things that lower your stress so that you don't get negative effects that change specific stats, as your character becomes more and more insane due to a heightened stress level they do various things. Character afflicted with the irrational trait will use moves without player input and characters who have become masochistic will jump at any chance to open something that might have a trap or hurt themselves instead of doing a player input action. Though raising the stress to 100 (out of a maximum of 200) could also give them a buff if they become inspired, ferocious, or courageous. It's a bit of a gamble when you do get to that point to see if you'll get a massive debuff and negative affects, or you'll get a massive buff and positive affects.
The game even allows you to cheat death by having a "Death's Door" effect, where every attack from an enemy has a chance of killing that character. I've used this function to get out of dungeons with all of my characters alive, though in major need ot stress relief.
The premise of this game is that you basically form a mercenary company.
If you like the writings of H.P. Lovecraft then you'll probably like this game, the same goes for if you like gothic psychological horror games.
So far it's a 7/10 for me.

Early game is pretty fun and fairly easy to advance through.  However, once you hit mid game (missions 5-1 and on), it starts to get increasingly grindy... or you can pay real money to expedite your advance.
That said, I was going to go through just to finish the game and get all achievements.  But I found out one achievement requires buying 2 trinket slot upgrades and 2 weapon slot upgrades - things you can only buy with energy (combined cost of 800 energy).  To get energy you have to pay cash (750 energy for $2.5) or you can exchange your crowns (game currency) for energy (~10,000 crowns for 100 energy).  You can probably raise about 10,000 crowns every 1-2 hours.  Additionally, the trinket and weapon upgrade slots only last 30 days - if you want them after that time, you'd have to get them again...
Another issue is you get to pick one of three pets as part of the 'story' progression.  Once you pick, you cannot change your mind - you are stuck with it.  However, it is possible to get other pets... at a cost of 2100 energy each.
The third issue is upgrading gear - a requirement for 'story' progression.  To upgrade one piece, you need three orbs of the correct level, but all orbs are very rare drops.  Mission 4-1 requires a set of 2 star gear (gear set = helmet, armor, shield, weapon - 2 star, easy enough).  5-2 requires 3 star gear (I saved time grinding by using 20K crowns to trade for 200 energy to buy a pack of three advanced orbs to complete my set).  Mission 6-2 requires 4 star gear... I only have one elite orb right now and need at least 16.  I can get packs of 3 for 400 energy each (total of 1600 = 160,000 crowns) or spend a few hours at a time to get a chance for one orb to drop.  Not sure which mission requires lv 5 gear, but those orbs cost 800 energy for a pack of three...  Leveling gear is similarily frustrating for level 3 gear and up - fire crystals drop more frequently than orbs, but you need a lot more to level up 5 pieces of equipment to level 10.
A few final notes: At times the game can lag a little - but if you are in a pack of baddies, you could find yourself dead without seeing yourself get hit (I died with full health due to internet connection lag four times in 50 hrs of gameplay.  Lastly, as you reach mid game the levels and baddies become a little redundant (especially with all the required grinding).
Also note that my perspective is primarily from a solo vantage - played a little co-op with a friend.  So I cannot comment on PvP or guild play or the like.
All considered, I cannot recommend this game as it gives you two options to progress once you reach mid game - grind tons of hours for little gain or pay chunks of cash.

Each different troop has a different potential to wreak havoc upon your unlucky solders and it make you prioritize them depending on the situation. A troop may be ignored as harmless given what else is in play but can also be the biggest threat another time. The aliens themselves are well designed and generally balanced(Unless you consider some of the new abilities gained as unfair).
As for the graphic design of the maps I have to say the devs did a stunning job. The randomly generated maps that are made for each mission to ensure no 2 missions have the same map is another wonderful touch. As for the story goes its well planned but contains several open ends as to why things play out as they do. As far as the "ant farm" on the Avenger is concerned it is the same with a few tweaks to building items and weapon/armor tier upgrades. Research is the same as Enemy Unknown but completely different from those of the last game.
The new classes are fun with all of the new combos and builds you can set up(i.e.; a ranger suited for scouting or being up close and personal). The combat itself is once again fun as it being XCOM you never know if a 1% shot will hit or a 99% shot will miss( both have happened , the missing the 99% more often ).                                                                                                                                                               	One of the largest things I`ve come to love is the modding support. I'm not going to lie when I say having a corgi gun to a Bob Ross  voice pack to having even more aliens and other little customizations of options added is one of the best things to happen. Being able to expand a game once all dlc is out will help draw out even more hours to the game play as you can combine and try different modded play-through.
With the recent patch out having fixed most if not all game breaking bugs and glitches,  making changes to video settings and optimatizations, and of course several small nerfs (mimic beacon). That and a  dlc relapsing on March 17 with several hundred more solider and weapon customizations is truly impressive.

Wow...I'm just blown away by this neat hidden gem of a game! So what's this game like? Well...it's like LoL but better...
First off you have ships: There are many different types of ships, your starters being your Flagship (a huge tank-type ship that's a beast in combat but moves like a snail).
You have your Corvette, which is basically a support ship with low attack but can heal other ships as well as put up some good harass.
and you have your hunter ship, which is pretty much a "capping" ship (basically it has good attack power with ALOT of speed).
So you're probably thinking "PFFTT, that's all!" but wait there's more! There are a variety of other ships to unlock (some of them are needed to unlock even MORE ships after you unlock the first one). For example, I just unlocked a ship called the "brawler", which is a ship that has a harpoon and can literally Scorpion pull other target ships to it and then unload on it with its plethora of short-range weaponry.
NOT ONLY THAT but you can also switch up the crew on your ship, basically each crew member comes with a bonus associated with them..some might give extra armor, more turning speed/speed on your ship, etc, not only that but there are other crew members that might give more attack/less armor, more turn speed but less regular speed...I think you get the point.
This is only scrapping the top of the ships available, there are LOADS of other ships with different weaponry and jobs.. but EVEN that's NOT IT. EACH ship, has unlockable different weapons to replace the default ones.. like for example on my capital ship there are usually attack drones, but I can unlock slow drones instead...to slow my opponent instead of doing damage to them.
I don't even mind the fact that there is no tutorial or training mode, because you don't need one...the controls are very easy to pick up and run great.. the ONLY curve I can think of is just knowing how to operate your ships weapondry and what each thing does exactly (this coming from a player who attempted to launch drones on a opponent who destroyed all my drones >.>).
Now those of us who have played LoL.. the worst part of that game is the community... WHAT CAN WE SAY ABOUT THE LoL COMMUNITY hmmm? Well they're a load of frickin' C*nts that's what we can say! A bunch of rowdy teenagers going around ganking with their frickin Ashe's and their damn Ryze's going 'HA, Pl0x No0b!!!!"  Well guess what in fractured space there's none of that... why? because you're WAY too focused on actually co-oping with your team to capture various points to trash talk... the closest thing to trash talk I've seen so far is the "GG's" everyone gives each other at the end of the round.
Look folks I loved LoL...I have a level 30 account on LoL even now, but let's face it the community is for little trash talking kids who want to feel good about themselves and rub their rank in everyone else’s face.
Look if you love the spacey-floaty feel you get in EVE online, and like the sotra MOBA-style setup of League of Legends GET THIS GAME NOW.
and don't let the "still in alpha" put you off...I’ve played quite a few matches and have found no glitches, the game runs smooth, plays smooth, is smooth.... 9/10 EVEN if I didn't pick it up on free weekend, if you're into LoL, buy Fractured space because it is TOTALLY worth your time to do so.

“The Skylark has been hit, sir!” one of the Knights cried out.
“Evacuate immediately! Nobody should be left on board!” came the orders of Captain Ozlo.
...And so the story begins.
-----
Spiral Knights is an MMORPG with roguelike elements and a scientific fantasy theme. You play as one of the Knights of the Spiral Order. Your primary function, before the crash of the Skylark, which was a massive spaceship, was to discover power strong enough to defeat your enemies in the Morai Wars on Isora, your homeworld. The Skylark picked up a major energy reading on a planet called Cradle. However, when the Skylark ventured to the planet, someone or something fired some sort of weapon at the ship, thus causing it to crash into the planet and partially explode.
Now, instead of finding a power source to save Isora, you are now looking for a way to fix the Skylark and return home. You aren't alone in this endeavor. Other crash survivors are also working towards the same goal.
Despite its welcoming name, Cradle holds many secrets. One secret is that of the alien species on the surface of the planet. Known only as Strangers, they have agreed to help the Knights by selling them equipment and materials. Other, darker secret hide below Cradle's surface though. Deep within the depths of the planet is a complex dungeon system known as the Clockworks.
Not much is known about the Clockworks. The Knights know it is constantly changing and that a race of aliens known as Gremlins live within the confines of the Clockworks. They are also are aware of the Core, which is in the center of the planet and was the thing giving off the energy source detected by the Skylark. Theories of the nature of the Clockworks vary from an experiment by the Gremlins to a museum of alien worlds absorbed by Cradle. Apart from the theories and facts, it is up to the player to explore the dungeons of the Clockworks and find a way off the planet.
-----
The game itself is really straightforward. Spiral HQ will give you missions that will teach you everything you need to know as well as give you ways to explore the Clockworks. These missions are divided up into different sections that will serve as tutorials and advance the story. There are also daily missions that will eventually get your prestige up (which basically gives you a spiffy symbol next to your name).
Another major part of the game is alchemy. Using materials you find in the dungeons, Bazaar, or Market, you can create weapons and armor that will assist you in exploration. There are currently five levels of equipment with one being the worst and five being the best. These levels, known as stars, allow you to gauge how well-suited (no pun intended) you are for a mission.
This equipment can be “forged” by collecting heat spheres in the Clockworks. One an item is fully heated after completing a level, you may use a Fire Crystal to level up your equipment. This is not the same leveling up that goes along with alchemy however. The equipment you use must be leveled up so many times using forging before it can be turned into a higher star using alchemy. Long story short, forging is a stepping stone used to better equipment in the alchemy stations.
Pets are another part of Spiral Knights. There are three types of pets that are conducive to certain playing styles. The first pet is a dragon that is predominantly used for offense. The second pet, being a cat, is mainly a support pet. The third, which is a phantom, is a combination of offense and defense.
-----
Fear not! You don't have to brave the Clockworks alone! Guilds and exploration parties are both commonplace in Spiral Knights. Banding together to explore the dungeons below is an excellent way to level up and have fun.
Guilds tend to be more formal than exploration parties. Depending on the size and seriousness of the guild, the guild may demand a few things from you. The guild has an “upkeep” cost that must be met weekly to keep the guild running properly. A guild also has the chance to purchase upgrades and decorations for their guild hall. That all comes with a higher upkeep cost though! A stricter guild will demand a certain amount of crowns, the in-game currency, per week from you whereas a lax guild could care less about how much you donate.
-----
All of this is wrapped up nicely with a beautiful soundtrack, cute graphics, player trading, a “stock market,” and frequent events.
-----
8/10
This game is amazingly good. It could do with some more updates and a bit more content, but overall is finely tuned game. I would recommend checking it out, especially with a few friends so you can all learn and explore together.

There are a number of issues that cause the game to show its age; Pushing objects is needlessly finnicky and sensitive, dead bodies do not let you walk over them until several seconds after their death animation, and every time you reload a game, it freezes your controls slightly after you start moving. But this is all minor compared to what is truly a spectacular game. It was named Game of the Year in 1998 for a reason.

I've gotten so many epics so far from mid range mob kills it isn't even a challenge anymore.
Trove is a sort of typical MMO mixed with Minecraft voxel based crafting and destruction.  So, if you like crafting games like Minecraft you will sort of like Trove.  It is a watered down Minecraft as there aren't as many things to craft initially until you level your crafting skills ala MMORPG fashion.
I dont know, I spent 3 hours playing one night and it flew by.  I had alot of fun just leveling my Frost Sage while trying to earn in game credits by doing achievements.  The in game credits can them be used in the cash shop or to buy new classes.    The game has been completely fair so far with the credits as I did very little to earn them other than do tutorial based quests.
There aren't quests in this game really.  It boils down to entering a zone, then farming dungeon after dungeon until you level.  Leveling doesn't take very long until you get to lvl 7.  To get to 7 takes about 20 minutes if you know what you're doing.  So it's a casual gamers paradise here.  On top of that, you will want to modify your cornerstone (home) and that takes time if you want it to look nice.
Honestly, the voxel based graphics aren't a huge turn off.  Within just a few hours, your avatar will look pretty bad♥♥♥♥♥
I'll keep this review very simple.  If you liked Final Fantasy or any strategy game, stay as far away as you can from this game.  If you liked Rygar without emulator saves, you'll like this.

Introduction:
First of all, I am not a native english speaker, so if there are mistakes do let me know and I shall correct them.
For real tho, this is my second most played game of all time, first being EVE Online with 1k+ hours (non steam). And with over 600 hours from the period of 4 years, I am safe to say I like this game. RotMG has gone throught alot of changes, which I have witnessed some, such as removal of ressurrection amulets etc.
Gameplay - to die or not to die?:
What comes to gameplay, it's a bullet hell arcade-ish grind. Realm might prove difficult to some people, or just content lacking, and those people usualy don't get very far. There is alot of progression, which unfortunately requires dying over, and over again. And ofcourse the endless grind for stat potions to make your character perform a little better with each sip. Overall, I like it after getting indepth with this game.
The game also features pets with many different abilities that benefit from your deaths, you die and you gain fame points that you can spend to feed your pet and make it stronger.
Oh, and most important, this game is permadeath, meaning you die, and you lose your character and it's inventory forever. However there is a vault to store your items you don't want to lose or keep in store for your next character.
Cash shop - pay to win?
Now you might be wondering, "well this is a free to play game, how is the cash shop?". First I'll say that people have alot of opinions on it, and I'll give you my own.
In no way I would consider this game 'pay to win', but throwing in 20€ for the starter package to gain a few vault chests and character slots does help you alot if you decide to stick around this game. There are also promotions of which are "3 character slots for the price of 2"-sort of deal. In my opinion, 20€ is very acceptable for a game, as I would consider the free to play option more as a trial.
The cash shop features useful items and gear for you to buy, but the game being permadeath I would not advice to buy equipment immedietly when you start incase you die. Also all of the equipment and more can be obtained by playing the game normally, since the item shop was added to the game years after the items were released. Everything, except cosmetic items and some other things can be obtained withing the game by playing it.
Lastly I would like to thank you for reading this if you did, and say that overall Realm of the Mad God is a very good game with balanced microtransactions. 9/10

=== WALL OF TEXT WARNING: if TL;DR, scroll down to the bottom to see a list of pros and cons. This is hastily written, otherwise, and may include: Foul language, sexual content, drug and alcohol abuse. Parental supervision is advised ===
World of Tanks meets Eve online. Save for the excel spreadsheet. Basically, space combat mixed with the WoT style turret and movement controls with the added (Spacebar up, ctrl down) Vertical axis. For those of you who like WoT, this is a try. It's a really nice and well-done game with a unique domination style/twist. Well, okay. Not unique. But how many games make domination fun?
First off, let me say this is a P2W game. Pay to win. As in you need to spend money, in the cash shop, to get awesome skins. If you don't like this, you should not play this game. It made me furious when I realized my new sparkly ship couldn't be that one awesome skin it didn't have because the Cash shop only has like 8 skins for the older/more-worked-on ships than my new Enforcer. So angry, horrible business motto. It's like they want me to lose because I don't look awesome- And you all know the rules! If you don't look awesome, you don't feel awesome. And if you don't feel awesome, you need to buy new pants. Looking good makes one powerful! But it's okay, my ship's black with many sparkly bullets and purple thrusters- I can pull through for a SHORT while. Seriously! It's like gameplay is more important than sparkly spaceboat pants! Guh! I want a black with lime-green spiral patterns on my Enforcer- In case any of you Devs are reading this!
Sarcasm aside-
Objective: Capture points down one sector or the other, two 'lanes', each with 5 stations. The stations closest to the bases(at the very end of the 'lanes') are like warpgates. You cannot warp to the enemy base until you capture these. On the way, between them, are some kind of- I dunno- resource stations? I think they're supposed to speed up/slow down captures depending on who holds them? Or maybe they contribute to how fast your team gets upgrades? Either way, they are a secondary objective for your team to grab. The main objective is to cap these big stations to warp to the enemy base. Then capture that and blow the crap out of all the enemies!
Combat: Your ship, and everyone else's is slow as all hell. The map is rather nice in size taking neither too long of a time, nor too short of a time to cross. Battles break out here and there, and this is a strategic combat game. If a gunship goes in alone against a frigate and a flagship, it's more than toast unless the pilot can pull off some really fancy dance moves- and I've had my fair share! It's intense. When you're getting hit, when you're targeting/focusing on a guy, chasing a straggler or wounded runner, or just trying to survive and capture until reinforcements warp in- It's damn intense. You have to know your ship, keep an eye on your cooldowns, pick your crew(Yes, you get to pick your crew), and keep an eye out for enemy ships, and red/blue dots on the map. There is nothing more satisfying in this game than hearing your ship's Captain tell you "Their core is breached, they're done for." And watching them get vaporized.
Graphics - I can say it's a pretty game. I give no missile volleys about the graphics here. The hell is Triple A, anyway? Fancy word for 'Game sucks, but you will buy for shiny graphics and blinding bloom!?" Yeah, now. Here, the graphics are nice, decent, and the bloom doesn't hurt my eyes. Good thing, too, because with all the fireworks, you need to not be blind to warp to the nearest frigate or corvette and blow their reactor right from under their butts!
Diversity is non-existant in this game. YET. IT IS ALPHA, PEOPLE. They're adding shiz, and you can fox right off if you complain about this- One map, 6 ships- NOT including the one in the Flagship branch because I can't count that high(If you must know, 6 for a total of 12)- and hardly any unique upgrades for most of those ships. What I mean is, the tech tree is currently limited- in ALPHA- and the hangar's customization- IN ALPHA!!- is limited. The basic 3 ships all have nice upgrade trees with each 'upgrade' having an upside and downside, rather than just being a 'better variant'. That is not to say you should expect the shinier ships to never get better upgrades. Yes, they're powerful, but the game refers to them in 'tiers'. So your choice. Get a ship that has no upgrades, but is still fun to use. Or use one of the older, basic ships and customize it for you. What will you do?
Matchmaking - None. Not yet. This is Alpha, after all, and they're just making sure the game works. I'm not sure, but I do believe they may implement matchmaking. There is a leaderboard, and there are rooms- servers- to join. But they're all labelled 'warm-up' and not 'ranked' or what not. So this tells me they're making the game, then fixing up a matchmaking. And if not- Still fun, but those poor newbies!
Tutorial/Getting started is kind of difficult. Tutorials are these videos on the front page that tell you the basics. It's nice, and all. But vague, and difficult to find when you're all; "OOOH, HANGAR! WHAT BOATZ I GOT!?" And click off. Seconds later I- err, the 'newbie' would hit launch and start a game with no idea of what to do... WTH IS THE WARP BUTTONG!? They cry, moments before they facepalm after realizing it's on the hotbar, bottom-center of the screen.
Progression is easy. Heck, I bought my new gunship- an Enforcer<333- in les than half an hour, in less than 4 games. Okay, well, 4 games. RNGEZUZ kind of gave me a 4,777 total, and unlocking a ship costs 5k. Also, 40k+ credits. Which I had around 6k exp/research/etc points, and a grand total of 60k creds. If you can't tell- THIS AINT NO LEAGUE OF LEGENDS! You can unlock everything easily if you really enjoy the game. Or upgrade the ever living heck out of your ship... if it has them.
Crew? I said something about crew? There's only a very little selection. Basically, Captain, Pilot, Comms, Tactician, Engineer, and I think I'm missing one, so they mustn't be imp- oh, right, you. The one who actually controls the ship! Riiight. Anyway, they each have 2 different characters per role. This is limited right now, but I bet the developers- SINCE IT'S ALPHA- will add more variety to the crew. Anyhow, each version of the crew's roles has a 'buff' they add. Such as a pilot's turn rate and max speed % each being different- I replaced my crazy russion pilot, Space bless his vodka-stained man diary, with a robot-cyborg-cat. Not a cat, but a tin can, really. Why? Because the bot ups my turn rate by 7% even though I lose the max speed that the russian guy gave me. And trust me. For the ship I pilot, that turn speed makes a difference- My ship is one that needs to shoot from the front. Oh, I should add that to the ship part of this review- Ships have roles, strengths, weaknesses, and if you get shot enough; Repairing won't fix the damaged armor!
TL;DR
Pros
- FUN for an ALPHA/EARLY ACCESS, Torpedo-sitters
- Really nice combat with a good emphasis on tactics, skill, positioning, communication, and map awareness.
- Easy to 'progress' and nice to 'experiment' with builds on ships that do have upgrades
- Interchangeable 'Crew' combinations that affect your... effectiveness in some small way(Which makes a much bigger difference than you actually would think- You can -feel- it while playing.)
- Game plays a little like a MOBA; As you fight and cap points, you get 'upgrades' that automatically apply once you vissit a large station or your main base( Upgrades Health, Speed, Fire Rate, and something else.)
- Graphics are shiny and dark at the same time! GET'CHER MIND BLOWN!
CONS
- ALPHA
- ALPHA
- Pay2pants
- Not for EVERYONE
- Limited customization
- Limited ships
- One map
- Hit and miss community
- No matchmaking system
- Free on Free weekend, yay!

Age of Empires III not only lives up, but pushes forward the great series that is Age of Empires. Most people compare it as being weaker than its predecessor Age of Empires II, but I find that these people tend to not see the greatness in this game. It seems in this Age of Empires the game became more realistic, in that the Colonial Era was a point in time when no longer were kingdoms limited in wealth by the amount of gold they could mine. Instead it brings in new Cash Crops, which allow each nation to produce Gold outside of traditional methods.
This is a great game with an in-depth campaign that goes through the stories of a Scottish Explorer and his sons/daughters. The campaign is interesting and introduces different styles of gameplay from macro-managing to micro-managing with scavenging and hording. Definitely worth the play through, for Age of Empires III and Age of Empires III: War Chiefs. Age of Empires III: The Asian Dynasties is fun, but the campaign has nothing to do with either of the other two expansions.
Age of Empires III offers a brilliant combat system that no longer requires precise delegation of finite resources, but allows for macro-scale battle. Allowing some players to turtle and others to expand, depending on your gameplay you can grow or stay at home. Mining gold and gathering food will always garnish better results than farming gold and food. Not only can you focus different resource harvesting strategies, but you can also use different strategies in your combat choices. You can buy mercenaries which cost only gold, or even capture native towns and create tribal units. This can allow you to vary your tactics based on your environment as well as your team.
This game introduces new challenges with Teams that are complex and highly differentiated, unlike in the predecessors where each team essentially was the same as the last minus a few shifts in upgrade options and one special unit (plus two special upgrades). Age of Empires III and its two expansions offer a variety of teams which include peoples of Europe, Americas, and Asia. Age of Empires III includes the Spanish, British, French, Portuguese, Dutch, Germans, Russians, and Ottomans. Age of Empires III: War Chiefs then offer three more teams including The Aztecs, Sioux, and Iroquois. Finally Age of Empires III: Asian Dynasties adds an additional three teams the Indians, Chinese, and Japanese.
If you actually want to enjoy this game make sure you edit your cities in order to get all the cards, as earning all the cards takes more than one lifetime. I have owned all three of these games before they were on steam and I put over +300 hours into it still to not have one civilization at maximum level.
If you enjoy real time strategy games, enjoy managing an economy, epic large battles, and don't like excessive micromanaging then this is the game for you. It offers brilliant combat with amazing scenery. The unit mapping is rather brilliant and the variety of maps keeps you constantly wanting to play more.
Pros:
+Fun campaign with a rather interesting story (for a strategy game).
+High level of variability in teams
+Allowing for turtle or rushing player types
+Good difficulty curve in AI (allowing boosting resource harvest rates to find the best balance of difficulty)
+Each civilization is like a whole new game
+On map bonuses to give reasons for exploring and moving quick across the map.
+Brilliant strategy diversification with special tribal towns on each map type, and special mercenary units for each map.
+Many different types of gameplay which keep the skirmishes from seeming repetitive.
+Loads of cards to choose from allowing you to choose if you want to Turtle, Rush, or Support.
Cons:
-Leveling civilizations is rather dull (just edit the text file)
-You cannot select your AI team members’ cards, which means they will just use resource cards, villagers, and soldiers (not team cards).
-Some civilizations seem unbalanced. (figure it out for yourself as we all have our views on this).
-Rather than producing names for the map choices they are named after states (which can be really hard to guess what type of map you will get if you're not familiar with US Geography).
-You can only have two teams in skirmish mode, which is really annoying if you used to like playing 2v2v2v2.
-You cannot have repeat civilizations; this means there is only one England per map.
