this is an incredible game!  There is tons of stuff to do, tons of stuff to micromanage, very good character development, a huge world, hundreds and hundreds of different types of in game items that you play with.  You will never ever not have anything productive to do.  The graphics may be on the older generation side, but in my opinion they are still fantastic for this type of game.  In simple terms some people call this game a farming simulator but it is much much much more than that.
However!!  The one and only thing that is absolutely [in my opinion anyways] bad about this game and makes it almost unplayable for myself and I am sure many others is the way time passes in this game.  Everything in this game is done on a regular 24 hours a day schedule, roughly 10 min. will pass for every 5 seconds real time.  There is no way to slow this down or turn this off or anything.  Time is always flowing.  Actually time does stop when you are not in the main gameplay window which you will be probably 99% of the time.  So in other words, if you are in the middle of playing and you turn your head in real life to talk to somebody or you go to the bathroom or anything like that game time will still keep flowing and within a couple of minutes half the day will be gone just like that.  And most things in this game need to be done on a regular schedule so wasting time like that is very detrimental!  I can't count how many times I have been distracted from the game for a minute or two only to turn back to notice half of the game day has passed by.  To me, that's the most important aspect of this game.  So unless you are able to 100% concentrate on the game without any external distractions then I recommend it very much, however if you're like me and you can't have 100% concentration/focus on the gameplay at all times than I do not recommend this game whatsoever.  It's really too bad game time automatically passes the way it does in this game, otherwise I think this would be a perfect 10/10.
But since it's not, I give this game 6/10

So, a lot of the reviewers for the game are giving it positive reviews because the devs have released an update. I felt like I should write a new review and focus less on the developers and more on the game that is available. I know a lot of you will look at my play time and think "He has X amount of hours in this game, he must have enjoyed it." But if I could have my hours back I would. Think of all those hours you spent in your last relationship and then try telling someone that the other person was worth dating and that you don't want a minute of your wasted time back. I tried to love it and I tried to be a beta tester and hunt down bugs, but it just wasn't worth it.
Right off the bat you'll notice that the game is very grindy.  Now, a little bit of grind is okay in a sandbox game as long as it's well paced and it never becomes tedious and boring; but Starbound does just that. The game becomes go from this planet to the next looking for another tier of ore and a boss to fight. You'll spend hours mining away, looking for the next ore. You run the risk of brain death while doing so, but it'll all be worth it in the long run, right? The boss fight and new enemies will be amazing, right? Nope and nope. Many bosses just feel like regular enemies on steroids, and the new enemies are just variations of the standard ones you see regularly.
Secondly, the game doesn't excel in any particular field. It's a jack-of-all-trades, master-of-none and each mechanic has been done somewhere else much better. Minecraft had better sandbox building, Terraria had less grind, more interesting bosses and a better sense of progression , and the combat is only adequate for what it is.
In the end, this game is merely a poor man's Terraria that manages to be more expensive. You're much better off playing that instead of Starbound.

Yeah, bread, very cute. But if you actually plan on being one with the bread, you'll have to face the challenges of being small and soft.
Making your way across a room is treacherous. Every bit of nasty filth you touch sticks to you. Climbing takes stamina, and when you're pulling a high-wire act above a groady pit of cat litter, the last thing you want is to lose grip just as you're about to make it.
The physics have a nice balance of predictable and wacky. Grabbing a freezer door with a little push can send you flinging across the room. Could be a time saver. Or you land in the sink. Losing control of the bread is typically amusing enough to help numb the pain of repeated failure. Plus there's an interesting freedom in being able to manipulate objects. You could theoretically roll yourself across the floor in a pan, set up a makeshift bridge, or rock a stack of boxes until they topple over. If one plan fails, there are alternatives.
The idea is to end up toasted on a heat source, evenly, maybe with some butter and jam. Whoever owns the house will come home to the perfect toast, oblivious that it gained sentience and went all Cliffhanger across their furnishings and refuse. Grandma's photo smashed on the ground, but it's cool. Toast.
Technically, the game runs a lot better than it did in Early Access, but it still needs work. My system seems to run a bit harder than necessary during normal play. Rampage mode is unplayable, with single-digit framerates. Other than that, it feels fine.

Black squad is a fast paced free2play PvP FPS shooter. It is a mixture between CoD and CSGO on "acid", with very very short time to kill (several 1shot headshot weapons, etc) and very fast movement (in-scoping and out). The game mechanics are quite good, weapons, recoil, nades (actually can kill you) feel good and realistic. The graphics are pretty decent too and the game is quite fluid overall. The maps are small and I mostly recommend doing (5vs5) demolition, plant the bomb, which is where the levels are better thought. The free to play model they have is quite ok and within a week you can get the most efficient weapons for you. On steam you can try the weapon download packages to get free trials of most weapons (which I recommend before getting any weapon for permenant), and afterwards you can invest in the ones you prefer.
Now with the major problems I have encountered which keep on appearing:
- I didn't know if to mention this because it's a "natural" occurrence in FPS games these days, but yeah, enough toxic people, and waaayyy to many "non-EU" in EU servers. *cough russians cough* so study those ruski insults because there will be many XD
- No ingame voice chat that makes it difficult to comunicate fast with the team-mates. So either get a full team of friends on discord/ts..etc or learn to use the team messages that are associated to several key patterns (still not fast enough sometimes). Also, dead team-mates' messages cannot be read by the living, but I can understand why they did that. I just feel that comunication is very important in this type of games, and a simple voice chat were you can mute, etc. would do.
- No kill cam with player outline. This is most important for the following problem.
- No report system AT ALL (at least I am still searching XD), which leads us to another big problem....cheaters... There are more and more each day. At first I thought I was a noob for not knowing the angles/corners/etc, but it is quite clear when you get hs through walls or prefired at ONLY when/where you are XD So yes, the killcam+report system are a necessity right now to be implemented or in a month this game will be unplayable. I was taking screenshots and calling out cheaters just to see that they didn't give a sh*t and laughed at me. Now I see why, if you can't report them, they wont get banned.
- No tier division based on rank. I mention this because the more experienced players are lightyears away from low ranks, and it is not fun for either to play eachother, just ridiculous.
So overall if the report-killcam is implemented I do recommend it, but until that, I just can't recommend it other than pass some time if you are bored of CSGO.
Hope this was useful for everyone, peace out.

So I buy this game in Early Access and it's terrible, right? And my characters get reset 5 times over right? So I drop it, write a terribad review for it, and use it as the reason I never buy any more early access games. But then I decide to come back to it later, how much later I don't give enough of a care to remember.
So I come back to it, probably because Snake bugged me to and said it was a good game. So I came back. So I made a new character, a starchild or whatever they're called. That's the first thing about this game: it likes to pretend that the differences between the races go deeper than their gameplay mechanics. Here's all the races
Human - generic generic
Apex - orwellian apes
Plantpeople - primitives
birdpeople - egyptians, occasionally muslims
robot people - medievals
fish people - nipponese desu (no not a mix of oriental cultures, just nips)
star people - cowboys
So these are all pretty creative races and what not, being that they're just ripoffs of human culture right? And I do mean ripoffs, I don't mean in any way that they were 'inspired' in any sense of the word, they're straight ripoffs. By the way, the story doesn't change if you start as a different race like they said it would be when the game was hyped up for those six figure salaries they wanted during Early Access.
But anyways, the story doesn't really matter outside of helping you have fun with the game, right? So first off you're always launched into this ridiculous planet tutorial where you have to go mine some core fragments and then rebuild your ship by seeking the help of Grandma Cripplelegs. I guess it works as an extended tutorial since you end up making a bunch of stuff to help you survive on the planet at first. So you mine the stupid core fragments, kill a bunch of stupid animals that look like pokemon rejects, and go activate the stupid portal so you can go talk to stupid Grammy Cripplelegs so you can fix your stupid ship. After you do the hideously boringly easy mission, you're off to explore the universe since there's no more stupid roadblocks in your way other than your own upgrade path.
Well, you'll come back to the story anyways because there's not a lot to do in Starbound other than go to planets and hope they're fun. You'll eventually and very quickly find out how fast everything begins to repeat itself, which can be expected in games like this. Since everything begins to repeat itself pretty fast, the act of exploration begins to become less fun until you go back to grammy cripplelegs for the story story. Well, the storystory is even more boringboring than the exploreexplore which is pretty boring after a few hours. Basically every single god-notforgiving story mission I've bothered to play through went like this:
1. go to planet
2. scan artifacts
3. report back to grammy cripple legs for the mission
4. play through easyboring mission with easyboring boss at the end
5. get a new homo companion who doesn't actually want to be a companion
So you go back to exploring because the story is dumb and stupid right? I guess the missions to get the mech and the tech were okay enough since they just involve some quick work, but the stuff you can explore with tech and mech gets pretty boring in and of itself in a short time. So you go explore more planets. Here's a rundown of what you'll expect going to planets.
1. every planet that's as lush as earth will have one random minor race in it and some human settlement
2. every planet more lush than earth will have birds/plantpeople on it and one other race settlement and frogs
3. every ocean planet has creatures that, darwin-rolling-in-his-grave forbids, can't swim for some reason.
4. every barren planet has nothing on it and they have no reason to exist other than to be barren
5. every friendly ship has nothing on it but free items in the locker
6. every random warp zone is a hostile mine field that leads to a broken down ship or an oddly hospitable tourists location
7. every enemy ship is filled with morons who will run headfirst into your mech's guns
I already got bored with the game at this point because it's a boring game surprise surprise. Terraria, which takes place entirely on one planet, manages to pull people in for a much longer time than this one. That might be because Terraria focuses less on exploration and more on a localized adventure, or it might just be because Terraria doesn't hide that it has terrible graphics. Did I mention the graphics? Everything is pillowshaded in this game and it all looks like it belongs on a sprite artist's tumblr where they post all of the work that they think looks good because they played one game on an SNES once and forgot what the graphics looked like so they decided that this was what retro was. I know the reason for this is because starbound can't afford pretty graphics like minecraft can (that was a joke) but the very least they can do is pillowshade it.
The combat in this game is really boring. Because the monsters are all focused on random generation (or else people would pick apart why there's so many similar monsters on different planets, which there is ANYWAYS) they're all focused on the same attack patterns which are incredibly easy to decipher. There's not a lot of room for interesting things like say a skeleton throwing his bones at you or a demon spitting fireballs because it all has to be based around a generic moveset or else illogicalities will start appearing in the monsters. This, needless to say, makes combat an absolute snooze. Hell, even the uncommon monsters that aren't randomly generated are snoozeworthy, taking for example the infected apex and that one onion thing that's stuck inside of a walnut, they're both TERRIBLY BORING and also both the most unique monsters I've seen in the time I was still not bored of this game.
I mentioned the story earlier and how each race has the same exact story regardless of what you want to do but I never actually mentioned what the story is and why it's so incredibly boring. You're a graduee from the Space United Nations and swear to protect everything in the name of Hillary Clinton and George Soros for the goal of space political correctness among 6 races (out of a possible, say, 100). Then suddenly the whole place turns into a hentai as tentacles attack and destroy everyone but you for some reason. So you get on a stupid ship and take off. Later you meet grammy crippleston who mentions that the planet was... Earth? Why Earth of all damn planets? Earth? God end me now. Anyways since Earth is dead and so are the Space United Abominations you obviously have to listen to Grandma nolegs and go do the stupid job of finding out what happened. Why not just hire a bunch of penguins to do it you may ask? because you need a job to do now shut up Anyways, so you do these boring and pointless things to find out whoever killed the dumb space UN and you find out it was probably some cult (wow, now we're making lovecraft references) led by a woman who I honest to god thought was a man because their sprite art is completely terrible and makes them look like a man. That's where I stopped playing and you can probably see why I stopped playing there.
I guess there are a few positives though. It gave me a fetish for girls who wear cowboy clothes. Seriously imagine if she roped you into bed and started taking off her duster, that'd be some kinky stuff. The idea of having a ship is pretty nice since it's somewhat of a 'portable home', alleviating the need to plop down brick and mortar on some planet and going back to it all the dang time.
tl;dr 'random generation' gets predictable fast but at least I have a degenerate new fetish

Having played this game for around 8,000 Hours (3,800 on this account, and 4,200 on another account) from Late 2011- Mid 2014, I must say it's been a great 3.5 years in the game. So great for me that I wouldn't say it's exaggerating that it has changed my life in many ways. (< Extremely irrevelant to the review though)
About the game:
Spiral Knights is a fun MMORPG game to be playing with a group of friends, completing the missions from the Storyline, collecting all sorts of unique Gear, Costumes and Accessories to customize your character's looks, or even merchanting in the game. (Merchanting is completely optional, but it was something that I've done for over 2 years in the game at least, and it was a good experience, getting to know more players, etc.)
Pros:
-A Wide Selection of Accessories to choose from, making your own unique costume
-Grinding (If you're into that sort of thing)
-Chatting inside and outside of the game
-Merchanting (If you want to include this from your perspective)
-Challenges for beginners
-It's Free!
Cons:
-Drops for specific items in-game is pretty rare, and players would sometimes just buy it directly from the Store, the Auction House or Players because they're not getting the drop.
-Once you've cleared everything, incluiding the DLC, you have pretty much nothing left to do, asides from collecting new gear and so on.
Spiral Knights from my Point of View:
Back when Nick was still in OOO, Spiral Knights was updated with a lot of new events, challenges, costumes, etc.
For PvE, My friends and I had a lot of fun clearing these challenges and grinding for the gears we so desperately want. Spiral Knights got a whole lot better when the Storyline was introduced, and the plot was interesting enough for us to keep playing, and we wouldn't get bored even though we're killing the same boss over and over again. (Well, that's what grinding in a MMO is about anyway...)
As for PvP, being in a different region from the Game Server will affect your gameplay for this game mode. But there are  people who're in the same state as me, but can dominate others. (Kudos to them, and no offence intended to anyone in this comment)
However, once Nick left, the amount of content for this game started to drop drastically, and I've only seen 1 or 2 major updates ever since he left. There are still updates to the game, but with just Accessories and Costumes, not much of content. This was the point where my friends and I had pretty much nothing left to do, after having almost everything we wanted. We came up with new ideas to entertain ourselves, such as time attacks for a certain lair, costume contests, etc. (I personally got so bored that I decided to design and make a whole ton of unique Costumes for my Character)
But after a while, all these ideas started to die down slowly, and I see a lot of Veterans and my friends leaving the game, and I've followed suit, and cashed out from the game, with almost no intention of coming back to play again unless I see an update which can convince me to play again. (I still love the game though..) I do visit the game occasionally, just to see how the game is doing, and everyone who're still playing the game.
The SK Community is one of the best Communities I've ever seen, and it probably would be. Players helping one another with problems, debates with just about anything related to the game, etc. As mentioned before, I'd hate to leave the game, but with almost no content, I see no reason of staying on.
For any beginner(s) reading this Review, I welcome you to have a go at this game, but don't be expecting too much unless you're into a lot of grinding for your desired items. :)
TL:DR
-A lot of grinding required, and pray RNG is with you when it comes to obtaining something you want from Boxes, etc.
-Intersting Storyline
-Fun with friends
-End Game is boring
Have fun, and may the Energy be with you!

I've been hyped for this game since its E3 showcase- Bethesda's first, actually. While they may not have delivered on their promises upfront, they made a concerted effort to correct the issues they found. While they may not have delievered on the hype, they did their level best to meet expectations and that hype was a result of my dedication to the IP for almost 20 years.
I've put more than a thousand hours into this game, almost all of them using mods. Mods and the Bethesda workshop were a major factor in my hype and expectations for this game. Now, they're the key reason I'm writing a review. The game's never been for everybody, but- from my perspective, of course- it's a title I would very much caution players away from.
You've probably already scanned the scores of other reviews that read simply, "PAID MODS!" They're telling an important part of the story, but not the whole story. I was sold on this game when it was announced, but I was only excited once I saw that showcase which promised mod support. This newest update didn't just introduce paid mods. It also broke the script extender which many mods rely on and included in its massive file size the .esp files for those paid mods.
What does this mean? It means that the next round of content that hits will require another download and update to the game files. This, in turn, means that the script extender will be outdated again. Not only will those using free mods be required to constantly update their mod library, but content creators will be struggling to stay with the current versions. Meanwhile, users of free mods will likely find their saves incompatible across seperate versions of the script extender.
This may sound like a Chicken Little scenario, but it outright ignores another possibility. With this being Beth's IP, they have a legal right and a vested interest in protecting it. Now, their mod workshop is another revenue source. If Activision-Blizzard is willing to spend their time shutting down private servers while being practically made of funding, how long do you think it'll be before Bethesda decides a cease-and-desist is a necessary step to protect their profit vectors?
Then again, maybe they removed the karma system from the game so they could pay more attention to it in real life. At any rate, I certainly hope this works out well for the modding community- you guys certainly don't deserve to get dragged into these kinds of fights.

I had a particularly heroic moment as one of my troops ran back, risking her life to save a fallen comrade. But as much as I reccomend this, I do have one warning: Very graphics intensive game, even on a decent machine. All things considered though, here's my scoring: Unmodded 8.5/10 Modded 20/10

I've been a fan of the XCOM games for a few years now. I'm not one of those veteran players that have been playing since Terror of the Deep or whatever, but I had a blast with Enemy Unknown, so I knew I was going to get this game. After playing this game enough to have a solidified opinion, I think it's easy to say that this game is a huge improvement over EU.
The graphics aren't actually that bad for a strategy game. The characters themselves look great, and environments look pretty. If you have the action camera on, then you photographers out there should get ready to take some nice screenshots.
If I were to explain the overall gameplay in one word, that word would be
The new classes (the Specialist, Gunner, and Ranger) are great replacements for the previous ones, and make the game far more interesting and teams much more diverse. My personal favorite seems to be the Specialist, because how can you NOT find using a drone to take control of your robot adversaries awesome? However, this is where one of the problems with the game seems to come in: there are some pretty rough balance issues here. Okay, first of all, I get that the game is supposed to be hard. I'm not talking about the enemies (besides the Viper and Codex) being over/underpowered, I'm talking about the XCOM soldiers themselves. The Specialist's drone is kind of underpowered when it comes to hacking the aforementioned robots, because the chance of actually hacking it is pretty low. The Psi-Soldiers are really OP, if you haven't heard that already. The Ranger's sword, although awesome, seems very situational. But, to make up for things like this, you have the new enemies. I don't want to spoil them all, but there's a few really creative ones that I'm a huge fan of. The pacing to the game has gotten some mixed reception, primarily because the timers can be really "unfair" in some cases, and this can actually be true if you're stuck on a mission where your target is on the other side of the map. However, the game is SUPPOSED to be hectic and fast-paced. You're running a resistance struggling to survive with the alien threat everywhere. You can't just run in guns blazing, can you? It makes the game a lot more exciting in my opinion. Also, the character editor is awesome. You like giving your characters more depth? Congratulations, now you can.
I haven't completed the story yet, but I'm pretty far into the game, and the story is actually pretty interesting. I'm enjoying my time trying to uncover the secrets of the Avatar Project, and the new characters have some depth to them, although they certainly don't reach points to other games. Not much else to say, but XCOM 2's story is surprisingly interesting to me.
There really isn't much to say here. The voice acting and music sound great. Obviously not to levels of other games, but this was not the category XCOM 2 was trying to excel in.
As I said before, I haven't completed this game. However, the mod support was a
good move. That gives XCOM 2 a LOT more replayability. Plus, the game is randomly generated in a lot of ways, so that might keep you interested for another playthrough. The only thing that might turn you off is how difficult the game is, it's fine to admit that the Sectoids can be really frustrating sometimes. *shudders*
As with most games today, there are a lot of bugs. Nothing game breaking, but minor ones that will make you want to repeatedly bash your skull into the wall. Luckily, however, that and the balance issues are the only major complaints I have about the game (aside from the perfomance issues at launch) and the game improves over Enemy Unknown in a lot of ways. If you're a fan of the XCOM games, buy it. If not, I would play some of the first game to pass the time while the game is patched. Overall, I'm a big fan of this game, and I'm looking forward to what happens next with my squad that pretty much fires every shot while blindfolded!

Starbound at first appearance appears to be Terraria in space. That's mainly because it is.
That being said, it's much, much more watered down compared to Terraria, which is quite disappointing, considering this game was in development hell for at least a couple of years. The mobs are pretty much the same as each other except with different skins (AI included), the planets have nothing to do on them apart from gather resources, the game's 'updates' are little more than art assets being added, and any negative complaints on Chucklefish's (or Chuckle♥♥♥♥s') forums get deleted.
Definitely don't buy the game in the state it is now. It's poorly coded, music's rather shoddy, gameplay is much more simplistic than Terraria's... possibly the only good thing about this game is the graphics, but even then, if you only care about graphics, you may as well go play an interactive movie like The Last of Us or Bioshock Infinite, which, despite being poorly made, are
better than this piece of crap.
Maybe one day, in the far-off future, it'll be worth it. But if it continues the way it is, it never will be.

The final installment in the Dark Souls series is one of my favorite games. I absolutely loved 1 and 2 (even though a lot of people crap all over 2, I still love it even more than 1) and I remember the day this was announced as I rushed to get my credit card and buy it. I own it on both PS4 and PC as a testament to how fun it is. Now let's put a hold on my personal experiences for a bit, and I'll get into why the game is fun and mechanics and such.
Now if you've never played a Dark Souls game, or anything from FromSoftware, don't despair as the games don't exaclty follow a story line and you can jump right in to the game. Beware though, Dark Souls is not for the weak of heart or those who are very easily angered. The game is tough, and it only gets tougher as you get farther in. You're going to die, you are going to get mad, and you are going to want to turn it off in a fit of rage. I'm pretty sure anyone who's played a Souls game has been there and done that. But the thing is, thats the fun of it! When you finally get past that enemy that always seems to see right through you, or you finally slay that towering boss who crushed you into the ground 100 times, you get so much satisfaction from it that you want to move on. I swear this game has turned me into a masochist, and I'm ok with that because I enjoyed every second of it.
So gameplay wise, the Souls series employs many RPG elements such as stats like Endurance, Vitality, Strength, dexterity, etc. that you level up as you go. The key to leveling up in the game isn't the typical experience bar that you fill through killing mobs or doing quests though. Every enemy you kill drops "souls" which are both used to strengthen yourself and buy things like upgrades or items. You can also use souls to strengthen the many weapons you'll find on your journey. There are several weapon classes each with their own movesets, stats, and requirements. All weapons scale off one of the  stats pertaining to damage like Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, and Faith. Your character also has stats like equip load that impacts your movement speed and rolling speed which is increased and decreased depending on what weapons and armor you have equipped. Theres actually so many more mechanics the game follows, but you learn those as you progress so i think this will stand as a decent outline for review sake.
Basically though as a sort of TL;DR The game is a pretty big, Somewhat open world RPG with a high learning curve that'll suck up so much of your time and rage and transform it into enjoyment. If you're looking for a challenge and something different than your typical RPG game, then look no further as Dark Souls 3 and any of its predecessors will have you covered. I actually don't feel like typing more for this review currently though, so if i remember I might update it later on. Anyways hope this review helped in some form, and I hope you pick up Dark Souls 3 and actually like it as it is an actually good game and I think everyone should atleast try it.

I like turn based strategy games and this game is held up as a benchmark for recent turn based strategy games. So naturally i would buy this when it comes out.
Cons:
A little too much animation for my liking - I don't see the need to witness the evacuation "mini scene" for each and every character evacuating at the LZ. If there can be some sort of shortcuts to mass evacuate all people in the LZ, it would feel less tedious, although i can understand why there is a need to evacuate individually.
Too powerful classes - the PSI skill domination is super OP. Once you have am operative that can use this skill, your missions got significantly easier. (I like getting pet Andromedons)
In comparison, the Hacker/Support class is more balanced in that Haywire Protocol duration is not infinite. Haywire Protocol felt like a more reasonably balanced way of diverting fire away from your beleaguered team in times of crisis compared to Domination.
I haven't figured out the utility of moving unseen - my teams always use the ambush tactic whenever the first significant target is within sights. I'll try ninja-ing my way though the next time.
Pros:
The game felt more tense - especially most of the missions have timers, forcing you to move aggressively (and create holes using grenades), so turtling is a less viable strategy.
The game tries to avoid the cruising experience by having in mission enemy reinforcements to liven up things.
The strategic game portion to advance the game by flying Avenger from place place to place got a little tedious when events keep disrupting your attention, ie Proving Grounds project completed, research completed etc.
The Heavy class felt more useful this time round. Grenades are indispensable when sprinting for the objective.
The last mission was really tougher compared to the last mission of XCOM. Was not expecting so much opposition.
Procedurally generated maps - more replay value. After playing too much of the previous XCOM, I can more or less predict the general location of enemies. So adding this feature is good for me.
I really like this game, will play more when i got more time.
p.s: I didnt encounter any graphical performance issues because I am used to running at low res. There's some jerking experience sure, but as far as i'm concerned it is secondary to the enjoyable gameplay.

Here is an honest review...
The game itself is great. It's basically what Cube World was suppose to be and more. If you don't know what Cube World was, then let me go ahead and just describe what Trove is instead. In Trove you can go into randomly generated worlds filled with dungeons and a scant few other interesting things. Clear dungeons for loot, mine for ore, fish, etc. The goal is pretty much just to level up and get the best gear, so it's not unlike other MMOs in that sense. The game also features some optional building elements (building a home/etc).
All of that being said, the game suffers from major server issues. Trion, the developers, are notorious for hosting their games on extremely low quality servers and Trove is no exception to this. "Rubberbanding", or the server lagging to the point that you are instantly reverted to your previous location from a few secions prior, is a common occurance. Waiting for the server to load the land infront of you is not in any way uncommon. The average ping you could expect to be playing is is anywhere from 200 to 1,000.  Now 1,000 ping may seem bad, but it's a hell of a lot better then when the servers are down, which is quite often. There is rarely a day that goes by when the servers are not shut down, without any warning might I add, for an hour or two. Pretty much every time the game is updated, majory or just by a hotfix, you should expect the servers to be down anywhere from 2 to 12 hours.

XCOM2 was the first XCOM game I'd ever played. I now own every (significant) XCOM game, and have completed most of them. The other games are incredible, and XCOM2 shares a lot of things with those games, but XCOM2 has a slightly more, personal touch, that really immerses you in the game. For example, character customisation is very big in the game, and even bigger with mods (full disclosure, my game is modded out the wazoo) so you grow attatched to your characters, and weep manly tears at their inevitable death. They also added (as you are an insurency group) wanted posters of your soldiers scattered around the map, making you feel as if you'd had an impact on the world. Alright, enough about the troops, and let's get to gameplay. The turn based combat is essentially the same as Enemy Unknown (2012), but adds a few new features: Hacking! Soldiers of a certain class can remotely hack network access points, giving your squad an advantage. Murderous robot about to blow up your squad? No worries, as Hackerman can stop it in its tracks, or even control it! Swords! As badass as it sounds. Emergency Evac! If♥♥♥♥♥♥really hits the fan, you can evac your squad, aborting the mission, and if one of your troops falls to the enemy, you can carry his unconcious body/corpse. I had a particularly heroic moment as one of my troops ran back, risking her life to save a fallen comrade. But as much as I reccomend this, I do have one warning: Very graphics intensive game, even on a decent machine. All things considered though, here's my scoring: Unmodded 8.5/10 Modded 20/10

I've been a fan of the XCOM games for a few years now. I'm not one of those veteran players that have been playing since Terror of the Deep or whatever, but I had a blast with Enemy Unknown, so I knew I was going to get this game. After playing this game enough to have a solidified opinion, I think it's easy to say that this game is a huge improvement over EU.
The graphics aren't actually that bad for a strategy game. The characters themselves look great, and environments look pretty. If you have the action camera on, then you photographers out there should get ready to take some nice screenshots.
If I were to explain the overall gameplay in one word, that word would be
The new classes (the Specialist, Gunner, and Ranger) are great replacements for the previous ones, and make the game far more interesting and teams much more diverse. My personal favorite seems to be the Specialist, because how can you NOT find using a drone to take control of your robot adversaries awesome? However, this is where one of the problems with the game seems to come in: there are some pretty rough balance issues here. Okay, first of all, I get that the game is supposed to be hard. I'm not talking about the enemies (besides the Viper and Codex) being over/underpowered, I'm talking about the XCOM soldiers themselves. The Specialist's drone is kind of underpowered when it comes to hacking the aforementioned robots, because the chance of actually hacking it is pretty low. The Psi-Soldiers are really OP, if you haven't heard that already. The Ranger's sword, although awesome, seems very situational. But, to make up for things like this, you have the new enemies. I don't want to spoil them all, but there's a few really creative ones that I'm a huge fan of. The pacing to the game has gotten some mixed reception, primarily because the timers can be really "unfair" in some cases, and this can actually be true if you're stuck on a mission where your target is on the other side of the map. However, the game is SUPPOSED to be hectic and fast-paced. You're running a resistance struggling to survive with the alien threat everywhere. You can't just run in guns blazing, can you? It makes the game a lot more exciting in my opinion. Also, the character editor is awesome. You like giving your characters more depth? Congratulations, now you can.
I haven't completed the story yet, but I'm pretty far into the game, and the story is actually pretty interesting. I'm enjoying my time trying to uncover the secrets of the Avatar Project, and the new characters have some depth to them, although they certainly don't reach points to other games. Not much else to say, but XCOM 2's story is surprisingly interesting to me.
There really isn't much to say here. The voice acting and music sound great. Obviously not to levels of other games, but this was not the category XCOM 2 was trying to excel in.
As I said before, I haven't completed this game. However, the mod support was a
good move. That gives XCOM 2 a LOT more replayability. Plus, the game is randomly generated in a lot of ways, so that might keep you interested for another playthrough. The only thing that might turn you off is how difficult the game is, it's fine to admit that the Sectoids can be really frustrating sometimes. *shudders*
As with most games today, there are a lot of bugs. Nothing game breaking, but minor ones that will make you want to repeatedly bash your skull into the wall. Luckily, however, that and the balance issues are the only major complaints I have about the game (aside from the perfomance issues at launch) and the game improves over Enemy Unknown in a lot of ways. If you're a fan of the XCOM games, buy it. If not, I would play some of the first game to pass the time while the game is patched. Overall, I'm a big fan of this game, and I'm looking forward to what happens next with my squad that pretty much fires every shot while blindfolded!

Black Squad is a unique gem, hidden in an over saturated market of F2P Shooters, and even FPS Shooters in General.
Let me explain:
The biggest complaint that most players ever have with F2P Shooters is their common tendency to become P2W. But, this game consistently avoids falling under that trap.
1. With in-game currency you can purchase weapons, weapons with attachments, and explosives (grenades, smoke grenades, etc.). These purchases can even be permanent, whereas most other F2P Shooters will only allow in-game currency to buy timed items.
2. This game has a surprising amount of Game Modes, even considering it's still in Early Access.
You have your Traditional TDM, Your "Search and Destroy" (Ex. COD Player here), and a new mode for me called "Battle Match". In my opinion, Battle Match is where this game truly shows the potential it can have as it goes through development.
Battle Match is a large-scale competitive mode that puts two teams up against 5 objectives that need to be destroyed. Dealing damage to the objectives will give you points, points can buy you Perks (Point Streaks/ScoreStreaks/Killstreaks... Again, ex. COD Player here) that are specific to the Class Style you choose to play with. This was way more content than I expected from a F2P Shooter.
3. This is probably minor to most, but I enjoy that this game supports a new way to engage in the Fast Paced genre with Sprint being mapped to the middle mouse key. Upon sprinting, the knife (or custom Melee Weapon) immediately becomes equipped and allows you to maximize the opportunity for Melee Attacks while swiftly moving around. It's a nice touch.
4. There is a pretty solid variety of maps that are exclusive to the Game Mode you are playing them on.
5. Lastly, which you would probably expect to be first but... Moving on: The Gameplay actually feels more solid than most of you would expect. Guns feel powerful, Movement feels swift, and the variety of Game Modes give a solid amount of replay value.
Now, even though I thoroughly enjoy this game, I would feel it unfair to not mention a few of the current cons:
1. Hackers.. They're only really on Battle Match, but when they come on... You really just stay away from Battle Match. What do they do? Turn fully automatic weapons into RPGS. Yeah...
2. Steam Controller support is non existent. Even mapping the keys in Big Picture Mode doesn't do anything. Most people on here will say it's a waste of time to play an FPS with a controller, but I highly disagree and always will. Please add the option to map keys to a Steam Controller, I know there's a few of us here that would appreciate that addition.
Other than that, I'm only 20+ hours in and have tons more playing to do. See you on Black Squad.

I honestly don't know whether to recommend this game or not.
On one hand, I love X-COM.  It's a great turn-based rpg that's carved out its own identity in a crowded field.  X-COM2 has improved many aspects of gameplay from its predecessor (i.e., soldiers on Overwatch no longer fire on simulataneously so you're not wasting ammo on corpses while other enemies run free), the maps have greater variety and the Character Pool allows you to stock your game with anyone you like.  John McClaine, Will Smith, John Cena, your friends or co-workers - just make characters for them and they'll show up randomly in the game.
On the other hand, the difficulty is punishing.  Not as bad as Dark Souls, but it's MUCH more difficult than the last X-COM.  With more than 100 hours of X-COM gameplay under my belt, I had difficulty keeping enough soldiers healthy enough to field a full team while keeping up with the game's Doomsday clock.  One of the new enemies that shows up early in the game clones itself each time it takes damage without dying.  It also dodges half of the attacks made against it and it has a lot of health.  And it has an attack that disables soldiers within a six-tile radius.  And it can teleport.  So when you see that enemy appear on the map when you have four turns left to achieve your objective, you might as well start over because you're going to be chasing clones all over the damn place.
In the middle, there's the added a concealment feature that allows your teams to set up guerrila-style ambushes as long as you keep your people in cover and don't tread too close to enemy positions, but this mechanic doesn't seem to work entirely well because my soldiers still get spotted despite following the expressed rules.  Also, I put the voice acting in his washout catagory.  The story is great and the villains are awesome, but the voice acting for two of the main heroes is abyssmal and there are way too many occassions when the game forces you to listen to the full term of their blathering before allowing gameplay to proceed.
All in all, I would caution the consumer to be aware before buying that gameplay will most likely involve a healthy dose of frustration, saving and loading and loading and loading...  but if you've got that A-type personality that loves this kind of Final Fantasy Tactics perfectionist gameplay, then it's a real gem.

I'm sorry this game, it's developers? They have problems. Look at this list here:
The developers are unable to take any criticism and the fans of the game are rude and sadly hateful preventing any constructive feedback from getting to them. At this point I can only strongly urge people to stay away from this game as it has the potential to be another Towns. I maybe mistaken, it could in a few years turn out to be a great game. As is? Not worth your time or money, and that is the bottom line.
As a note: It remains such a heavily played game on Steams watch list because the developers haven't fixed a "bug" where the launcher stays open or sometimes the exe even when you close the game. Shady when this has been reported to them numerous times since this alpha released in December.
Edit: It has been a a bit now since I wrote this review and thought I might expand on it a little now that they have released a nightly build feel I should expand on the gameplay itself some. I didn't touch on it in my first part but focused on the larger problems, and plan to correct that now.
At the core, the game itself is at present a stripped down Terraria. It may generate planets, but all these are is procedurally generated worlds just like Terraria. Only, rather then most of all biomes in one world they have maybe two biomes per world. Other then that worlds are bland and fairly uninteresting. There maybe generated villages but all these are good for is grabbing decorative items.
Next on the list is combat. The combat is, even in the new nightly, clunky. A borrowed shield mechanic from Secrets of Grindia doesn't really help matters much. The monsters are all spazy with little variations despite the procedural generation nature of them. Also healing becomes an issue the higher in tier you go.
Exploration, or.. why Terraria blows this out of the water. Every item in Terraria has a use that you find early on. Every biome has reasons to visit it. Every npc has a reason for being besides background fluff. The major difference between them is you feel rewarded for exploring in Terraria. Starbound throws out tons of things at you but none of it feels as exciting as when you get a hook item or magic mirror in Terraria, because these things have a use. They have meaning that makes exploration worthwhile.
Now when it comes to fluff the game itself has some serious issues with bloat, lack of direction, and speed of development. The pokemon like mechanic is somewhat of an interesting idea but is half implemented and not done well. The expanding ships are not customizable, the various biomes are pallet swaps. The list goes on of fluff, while core things like selling items and various other necessary mechanics have at the time of this writing been left to gather dust. The whole "story in a sandbox" is a big selling point, and there is no story almost to be found!
Given how slowly the team works as the game has not changed hardly at all in seven months.. we are left with many things unfinished while they work on silly side items rather then the main progression path.
The game has spent three years now in development, and does not show it at all. It still remains not worth your 15. Also as of this spring chucklefish stopped allowing refunds, despite the assurance they always would. Further shady dealings with a team that has made millions and is hardly making any progress at all.
Edit2: The 2014 very end of the year winter update of restriction.

Hoo boy... I am Bread is a game that makes me feel stupid. I mean, I liked it, but it's hard to say WHAT I liked about it.
Gameplay: The main meat (or should that be Wheat? Yes, I am Bread and its players are all full of crappy puns like this) of the game is the main mode. You are bread (duh) that can hold on to objects by its corners. Your ultimate goal is to reach a heat source and toast yourself 100% on both sides, whilst keeping away from the floor or anything that could possibly spoil you. If your edibility drops to nil, that's it. Of course, getting to the end is easy enough by this game's standards. If you want a good rank, you'll smear some spreads on yourself (the bread, you dolt, not YOU) and pick up some tasty things along the way and do your damndest to keep your edibility from going down, along with doing all of this in a timely fashion and making sure you don't burn yourself. Only then will you obtain the coveted A++ rank.
Controls: One of the biggest points of contention with this game are its controls. By default, a keyboard has you use 1, 2, 3, 4 and the arrow keys to grab on to things and move around as well as Q, W, E and R to hold things, along with the mouse to move the camera. A controller will have you use the four shoulder buttons and the control sticks to move yourself and the camera around. It also uses the four face buttons to hold on to things. Leaning towards using a controller? Good, since that's the way the game really should be played.
But hold on. Let's not be silly. You can't just hang on to the ceiling all day like a bread bat. You have a grip meter in a manner reminiscent of Shadow of the Colossus. If that runs out, you drop off of what you were holding on to and drop what you were holding. Anyway, that said, the bread controls quite oddly. Don't expect to sit down and be able to control your bread right away. This takes time, and even then you may still struggle a bit. Because this game and its controls are seriously difficult.
Adding on to the above, it seems that few bugs may have slipped through the cracks in Early Access. For instance, don't be surprised if your bread gets stuck in something, and the fixing of it sends it flying through the air having a seizure, ruining what you've just done and forcing you to start again.
Still, despite this, don't get me wrong, the game is still quite a lot of fun (it's also massively frustrating, but still). You have multiple modes to play with, with seven different levels to mess around in. You have Cheese Hunt (you play as a cracker), Rampage (you play as a baguette), Zero-G (you play as normal bread with rockets all over you, no joke) and Bagel Race (no♥♥♥♥♥♥. Each mode has its own objectives, and each level has its own ways of cooking yourself. Some of which require some thinking. Seriously, you'd be surprised at how much of an actual game this is, rather than just a piece of shallow Youtube fodder/PewDieBait. Is it worth its current price? Maaaaaaaaybe. That's down to you, since there's quite a bit of content (albeit the same seven levels in five different scenarios, so not counting the free roam, you'll have 35 levels to keep you occupied), but as was mentioned above, it is majorly rage-inducing. Even so, whether on sale or at full price, give I am Bread a
TRY sometime

At first, this may seem like a simple joke simulator meant for a quick cash-grab from Let's Players.  That is decidedly not the case here.  While the premise - a slice of bread journeys to become toast - is indeed ridiculous, I am Bread does not rely on its absurdity.  Rather, it uses its outlandish premise as a guise for challenging and immensely rewarding gameplay.  Much like they did with Surgeon Simulator, Bossa Studios gives the player more controls than they are probably used to: you will need full analog control and eight buttons to maneuver your piece of bread around the terrain.  This quickly becomes second-nature, though, and the game relies more on using interesting mechanics to solve puzzles than simple "LOLphysics" gameplay.  You may be a veritable bread ninja, but unless you can find a heat source you shall never become toast.
Once you have the basics down, becoming toast simply isn't enough; you must become *delicious* toast!  Who wants to be dry toast when there is butter and jelly available?  Sure, being slippery or sticky may impact your ability to navigate, but you get to be tasty!
I cannot, in good conscience, reccomend Fallout 4. the game itself is fine, but the addition of paid mods is not.

I'm sorry this game, it's developers? They have problems. Look at this list here:
The developers are unable to take any criticism and the fans of the game are rude and sadly hateful preventing any constructive feedback from getting to them. At this point I can only strongly urge people to stay away from this game as it has the potential to be another Towns. I maybe mistaken, it could in a few years turn out to be a great game. As is? Not worth your time or money, and that is the bottom line.
As a note: It remains such a heavily played game on Steams watch list because the developers haven't fixed a "bug" where the launcher stays open or sometimes the exe even when you close the game. Shady when this has been reported to them numerous times since this alpha released in December.
Edit: It has been a a bit now since I wrote this review and thought I might expand on it a little now that they have released a nightly build feel I should expand on the gameplay itself some. I didn't touch on it in my first part but focused on the larger problems, and plan to correct that now.
At the core, the game itself is at present a stripped down Terraria. It may generate planets, but all these are is procedurally generated worlds just like Terraria. Only, rather then most of all biomes in one world they have maybe two biomes per world. Other then that worlds are bland and fairly uninteresting. There maybe generated villages but all these are good for is grabbing decorative items.
Next on the list is combat. The combat is, even in the new nightly, clunky. A borrowed shield mechanic from Secrets of Grindia doesn't really help matters much. The monsters are all spazy with little variations despite the procedural generation nature of them. Also healing becomes an issue the higher in tier you go.
Exploration, or.. why Terraria blows this out of the water. Every item in Terraria has a use that you find early on. Every biome has reasons to visit it. Every npc has a reason for being besides background fluff. The major difference between them is you feel rewarded for exploring in Terraria. Starbound throws out tons of things at you but none of it feels as exciting as when you get a hook item or magic mirror in Terraria, because these things have a use. They have meaning that makes exploration worthwhile.
Now when it comes to fluff the game itself has some serious issues with bloat, lack of direction, and speed of development. The pokemon like mechanic is somewhat of an interesting idea but is half implemented and not done well. The expanding ships are not customizable, the various biomes are pallet swaps. The list goes on of fluff, while core things like selling items and various other necessary mechanics have at the time of this writing been left to gather dust. The whole "story in a sandbox" is a big selling point, and there is no story almost to be found!
Given how slowly the team works as the game has not changed hardly at all in seven months.. we are left with many things unfinished while they work on silly side items rather then the main progression path.
The game has spent three years now in development, and does not show it at all. It still remains not worth your 15. Also as of this spring chucklefish stopped allowing refunds, despite the assurance they always would. Further shady dealings with a team that has made millions and is hardly making any progress at all.
Edit2: The 2014 very end of the year winter update of restriction.
I'm only going to touch on this shortly for now. The developers have finally put in the framework for quests/missions. Ones however, that bring you out of the sandbox. Only as a way to restrict your progression for the most part as well. You are now metaphorically bound to a hubworld as they are along with most things of importance now set outside the sandbox, where you will find tech that allows you to explore planets after doing a bunch of run around more or less. Also they have removed several features such as temperature and hunger at the time of this writing. Main progression path still doesn't have as much done as should be after a years worth of effort without any sort of effective communication from them on steam.
The game is becoming a non-sandbox restricted game with block building tacked on and features being moved to post release, later, or culled all together. I believe this will be my final update to the review until the full release. I still cannot in good faith recommend this game. Not because it is incomplete but how it is being handled and where it seems to be going along with the scant little still in it. The developers spent almost a year not listening to feedback while also not even managing to put in content that modders did in weeks after the beta dropped. The final result of it all is a less open exploration, chore to play "game", then what was there months ago.
If this is the future of Starbound, it looks bleak.

This game is as hard as it is gorgeous and I can surely say that I've never played a game that is as unique as this one.
One of the best things in Darkest Dungeon (in my personal opinion) is that unlike most turnbased RPGs it is possible to assemble a team of 4 members that you can customise to suit your own playstyle or try out a different startegy.

Simple, addictive fun. This is easily the most approachable MMO I've every played. It's simple: shoot whatever is shooting you. There are many classes in the game, each unlocked by leveling up the class before it. You can carry up to 8 items at a time, which may seem small, because it is. I'd say this is a good thing though, since all you ever really need there is potions. Any items that you find that your class can use can be immediately equipped over what you currently have. There are 4 equipment slots: one for a weapon, class ability item, armor, and ring. So you'll only ever have to deal with 12 items, tops. This is great so that you can just focus on your shooting. There are quests, but they are really just a specific enemy you ought to kill, pointing you to their direction, and they usually have a whole bunch of minions to defend them . Every time you complete a quest, you immediately get another one, so you always have something to do. Also, permadeath and cute retro graphics.

Words of warning:
1- The game is poorly optimized right now, I had many crashes during ship view mode, the solution was to choose low graphic settings.
Even with high settings the game runs fine for me in tactical mode, but I was getting lots of CTD, even when my spec are the reccomended.  This problem is awknoledged by the community manager, but I don't know if it's awknoleged by Firaxis itself.
2- There are mods aplenty, but once you save a game using a mod the save won't load if the mod is disabled. There are ways to disable mods via configuration so it looks enabled but does nothing, just a dummy mod, which is a dirty solution but is the only solution if you have a save with a mod and don't want to use it anymore.
So make a backup save before installing any mod so you can have an easy rollback in case you don't liked the mod.
The rest of the game is pretty good, pretty much the same to XCom EU with improvements and new mechanics here and there.
The only thing I didn't like is the extra pressure of having limited turns in most missions. Whenever there is a mission without any kind of time pressure is a relief.
The turn limit is so tight that you have to choose to rush in the early turns, throwing caution out of the windows and risking deaths, damage and panic; or you can choose play cool at first and rush later only to find yourself with 2 turns left and heavy enemies between you and the extraction zone, risking leaving soldiers behind. Pretty much a lottery.
Many people liked that because it's an extra pressure element. But if you think like me, the game already have enough pressure without the tight limit, luckily there are mods to aleviate this. The ones I saw come in many flavours, one disable the turn limit, another adds some turns to the limit, the one I picked lets you configure how many extra turns you want.
Overall the game is as good as the previous one, a pretty good turn strategy game. I just hope they fix the optimization problems

I currently don't like it's current representation. I'm not a godlike player and I'm pretty casual but some things about this game's mechanics honestly frustrates me that affects the whole core experience. I've only 2 games under me, I'm currently at 1.3 KDR. For a newbie with less than an HOUR, I'd consider it pretty decent.
That said, let's bring light into some issues.
Aiming:
It's not capable of "hold ADS". It's completely toggle and it get's worse on guns with 2 seperate sight mods that isn't a sniper rifle like the game's representation of the SCAR-H.
It has 2 sight attachments, one red dot sight and one 4x(?)  sight. You want to aim at a guy on a rooftop? Sure enough, 4x comes first and that can be respectably handled. Done shooting him to death, you want to aim out and guess what... you switch to your red dot sight on the 2nd right click.... okay, that doesn't sound to bad and you click again and back to hipfire...
Next thing you know, you're getting jumped close range and BAM, 4x scope, sensitivity a bit haywire and you're overcompensating so you right click to red dot sight and either you managed to kill him or die.
Now imagine that for the entirety of the match.
But that's not all, it's completely spastic in it's aim mechanics itself meaning, if you right click, sometimes you zoom in toggle but other times out of nowhere, it ACTS like it's "Hold ADS" and zooms out after that right click... What???
So you're options are to either:
Scope in for the majority of the match with some actual zoom like the majority of scopes on sniper rifles or the 4x on the SCAR-H
or
Hipfire like it's an arena shooter.
Sprinting / Melee:
You want to move fast? Use your knife, only, it's not like CSGO... you HOLD the middle mouse button.
HOLD. Not Toggle... but HOLD... why this isn't properly implemented for aiming (considering there's actually *2* keybinds for Aim Toggle: Right click and... U... but why though?????)
So you hold the melee to move fast... In a game where guns have "mobility" stats that give players an innate advantage over lower mobility guns that players want to use. So when you're using a sniper rifle, holding down that melee button, you see a player with an SMG zoom past you with their gun at the ready... while you have a knife out that can barely keep up.........
So here's the positives:
Currently in it's representation, there is no P2W. Yes there is exclusive guns/characters that can only be purchased with real $$$ but you are arguably starting out with the best and balanced weapons.
Graphics are good
Hit detection is really good
Sounds is bland and expected out of most F2P FPS.

In XCOM 2 Earth forces have failed to stop the alien invasion of the first game and entered a pact with the invaders: most people now believe the aliens to have peaceful intentions and are happy to let them control most of their life. The XCOM project is still alive though and is trying to mount a resistance movement to find out the aliens' true agenda before overthrowing their government.
The game is both an overhaul and a refinement of its predecessor and stands out as the finest XCOM game in recent times despite a shaky release.
-the overall graphics are pretty good with nice effects and animations
-good soundtrack
-while pretty cliched the plot flows well and there'd a decent amount of mistery behind the aliens' plans
-the new resistance-styled XCOM really has alot of character and charm
-still sports some top notch turn-based tactical combat made even better by added mission types and better level randomization
-the concealment mechanics are truly superb and provide good tactical depth
-new soldier classes are excellent and great to use: said soldiers are also fully customizable in their looks, voice, stance etc
-moddable weapons are fun
-new alien types are quite interesting and can surprise you with some new abilities, their design and animations are also great
-good length, each campaign'd last you at least 20/30 hours
-timed missions can be challenging or annoying, also depending on personal taste: still there's mods to make timers longer or remove them altogether
-some missions can feel a bit unfair in regards to the amount of enemies thrown at you
-uneven performance
-long loading times
-some line of sight bugs (like through closed steel doors) can be annoying and ruin your tactics
-camera can be problematic at times
-still has several bugs (a few crashes, audio desync in cutscenes, envirnment destroying itself for no reason etc...)
Going from a worldwide funded organization to a small resistance movement is quite a change and while I wasn't fully convinced at first I must say it works perfectly: you'll feel like a guerrilla squad operating behind enemy lines, facing overwhelming odds and slowly turning into a truly badass spec ops squad as time goes by and promotions mount up.
The new mechanics Firaxis introduced provide an overall better game experience both in the field- with concealment letting you decide when and how to start going guns blazing, soldier skills providing many ways to get the upper hand over the aliens and synergizing well with each other, etc- and in the geoscape view- with mutually excluding missions prodiving different bonuses and drawbacks, POIs to explore, the Avenger to rebuild and so on. There's just so much to do, most of it is fun and well-designed and the game's brand of challenging, deep combat is simply as outstanding as it is engaging.
There's a few dents into this great game sadly and most of them are due to a shaky release. There's some line of sight bugs where you can be discovered through solid walls and closed doors,a few AI hitches, shaky framerate, some jarring problems with audio in cutscenes getting messed up and the game can sometimes simply crash to desktop. Even after a patch things havn't improved too much so here's hoping Firaxis gets their act together and finally polish everything up.
Even with all its blemishes XCOM 2 is simply an impressive entry in the franchise and a must buy for both long-time fans and newcomers: it's that good and it's only going to get better through patches, mods and DLCs.

Starbound is an unfinished game, and there is no grantee that it will ever be finished. Even if it is ever finished and reaches a 1.0 status release, I don't think it will ever be the game it was hyped up to be.
While the game in the current state is playable and initially showed strong potential, development progress has come to a near standstill, and there are significant problems in the existing product. You might get 20 hours of play time from Starbound, but it doesn't have much replay value.
Since the game was published as Early Access in 2013, there has been very little progress in game development, programmer (Bartwe) and artist (Rhopunzel) have left the company, and there have been a number of serious incidents which call into question the honesty and moral integrity of Tiy and his company. In mid-2014 there was a nine-month period with no updates at all. 2015 has been fairly similar.
The amount of progress which has been achieved over the years is damningly small. This is a company that took in millions of US dollars in pre-orders and has at least a dozen staff members. What are they doing all day?
Chucklefish has a blog where they show off development progress, but it's mostly PR and photoshop mockups. They hope to convince players that progress is really happening and that some day, the magical update of their hopes and dreams will arrive.
There have been incidents in the past where they would publish updates which had wiped characters and destroyed items, ala the Feb 19th 2014 "chest apocalypse".
The events including the repeatedly broken delivery date promises, Bartwe and Rhopunzel's departure, Omni's mass-banning incident, other censorship and community dishonesty issues, the nine months with no updates to the game, and other toxic community drama should scare any reasonable person away from this title.
I've gone from hope to pessimism to just moving on and leaving it behind. Starbound will almost certainly never be the game I had hoped it would be.

and there lies the catch....... the upgrade "tokens" can all be bought for real money.
I can log in on day 1 with 30$ and have the equivalent of level 200 gear on the game.
I can log in on day 1 with 30$ and have any mount , cosmetic costume, gear, blocks, anything in the game with real money, as well as the strongest gear + upgrades.
Thats where this game hit a dead end for me. The building is much less intricate then minecraft. No moving parts (redstone) and no textured blocks. Just flat cubeworld blocks. The gear is buyable. The worlds are instanced so you totally lose that feeling of immersing your self in the same world as everyone else.
All in all 7/10
With all of that being said, In playing this, you can almost imagine the perfect video game and what it could be. Game developers are nearing the recipe that could appease both the building/artistic ascpetcs and RPG/MMO aspects all at once. The game just hasnt hit yet. Words of warning:
1- The game is poorly optimized right now, I had many crashes during ship view mode, the solution was to choose low graphic settings.
Even with high settings the game runs fine for me in tactical mode, but I was getting lots of CTD, even when my spec are the reccomended.  This problem is awknoledged by the community manager, but I don't know if it's awknoleged by Firaxis itself.
2- There are mods aplenty, but once you save a game using a mod the save won't load if the mod is disabled. There are ways to disable mods via configuration so it looks enabled but does nothing, just a dummy mod, which is a dirty solution but is the only solution if you have a save with a mod and don't want to use it anymore.
So make a backup save before installing any mod so you can have an easy rollback in case you don't liked the mod.
The rest of the game is pretty good, pretty much the same to XCom EU with improvements and new mechanics here and there.
The only thing I didn't like is the extra pressure of having limited turns in most missions. Whenever there is a mission without any kind of time pressure is a relief.
The turn limit is so tight that you have to choose to rush in the early turns, throwing caution out of the windows and risking deaths, damage and panic; or you can choose play cool at first and rush later only to find yourself with 2 turns left and heavy enemies between you and the extraction zone, risking leaving soldiers behind. In XCOM 2 Earth forces have failed to stop the alien invasion of the first game and entered a pact with the invaders: most people now believe the aliens to have peaceful intentions and are happy to let them control most of their life. The XCOM project is still alive though and is trying to mount a resistance movement to find out the aliens' true agenda before overthrowing their government.
The game is both an overhaul and a refinement of its predecessor and stands out as the finest XCOM game in recent times despite a shaky release.
-the overall graphics are pretty good with nice effects and animations
-good soundtrack
-while pretty cliched the plot flows well and there'd a decent amount of mistery behind the aliens' plans
-the new resistance-styled XCOM really has alot of character and charm
-still sports some top notch turn-based tactical combat made even better by added mission types and better level randomization
-the concealment mechanics are truly superb and provide good tactical depth
-new soldier classes are excellent and great to use: said soldiers are also fully customizable in their looks, voice, stance etc
-moddable weapons are fun
-new alien types are quite interesting and can surprise you with some new abilities, their design and animations are also great
-good length, each campaign'd last you at least 20/30 hours
-timed missions can be challenging or annoying, also depending on personal taste: still there's mods to make timers longer or remove them altogether
-some missions can feel a bit unfair in regards to the amount of enemies thrown at you
-uneven performance
-long loading times
-some line of sight bugs (like through closed steel doors) can be annoying and ruin your tactics
-camera can be problematic at times
-still has several bugs (a few crashes, audio desync in cutscenes, envirnment destroying itself for no reason etc...)
Going from a worldwide funded organization to a small resistance movement is quite a change and while I wasn't fully convinced at first I must say it works perfectly: you'll feel like a guerrilla squad operating behind enemy lines, facing overwhelming odds and slowly turning into a truly badass spec ops squad as time goes by and promotions mount up.
The new mechanics Firaxis introduced provide an overall better game experience both in the field- with concealment letting you decide when and how to start going guns blazing, soldier skills providing many ways to get the upper hand over the aliens and synergizing well with each other, etc- and in the geoscape view- with mutually excluding missions prodiving different bonuses and drawbacks, POIs to explore, the Avenger to rebuild and so on. There's just so much to do, most of it is fun and well-designed and the game's brand of challenging, deep combat is simply as outstanding as it is engaging.
There's a few dents into this great game sadly and most of them are due to a shaky release. There's some line of sight bugs where you can be discovered through solid walls and closed doors,a few AI hitches, shaky framerate, some jarring problems with audio in cutscenes getting messed up and the game can sometimes simply crash to desktop. Even after a patch things havn't improved too much so here's hoping Firaxis gets their act together and finally polish everything up.
Even with all its blemishes XCOM 2 is simply an impressive entry in the franchise and a must buy for both long-time fans and newcomers: it's that good and it's only going to get better through patches, mods and DLCs.

TLDR : This game is a lot of fun and frustration and you have to like the art style to fully enjoy it.

Aside from that, it's a three dimensional platformer in which you're a piece of bread that needs to be toasted either by a toaster or a heat-transmitting object. If the bread comes into contact with certain objects such as the floor or inedible loose items around the map, it loses edibility which is calculated into the score at the end. The bread can also over cook if it is left toasting too long, or if it is not toasting the whole side of the bread evenly. Controls can be a bit flimsy at times, but many bugs have been fixed and shouldn't occur.
I do recommend this game for its general humor, original gameplay, and toughness for newcomers. The music is very fitting and catchy, the game is fun, and you're going to love it.

I'm not usuially a review kind of guy, but this game is something special and deserves a review.
Darkest Dungeon is not a game for those who can't deal with the concept of every single action having a major concequence, either positive or negative, in the big scheme.  This game WILL push you as an individual and at times it will make you question your desicions and morals.  The game itself comes with a warning that it is a game "about finding the best possible outcome of a bad situation".
That being said, I don't regret a minute I've played this game.  I loved the struggle the game puts you through, and the constant threat of a situation going sour keeps you on your toes, even past the initial shock of the game.  I've completed most of the content in the game, but every time I do a new quest it always feels like a brand new experiance.  Thanks to the unique combat system and the randomized dungeons, the game doesn't begin to feel repetitive.
Lots of people have put in negative reviews on the basis that "RNG KILLED MUH PEOPLE", and to an extent they are right.  This game makes you feel very bad about losing characters, and since there is no way to get them back a character who you've built up over the past 10 hours might be subject to dying at any point in time.  It's rough, but that's part of the beauty of Darkest Dungeon.  Very few other games on the market force you into this type of situation, and even fewer prevent save scumming to get them back (yep you read that right, if you lose someone you can't cheat the system).
All together, Darkest Dungeon is absolutely worth the $25 full price, and if you can get it on sale consider yourself lucky.  It's one of my favorite games from recent years and I think it'll stay that way for a long time.
