This is a blatant advertisement for my favorite HL1 mod Action Half-Life, this mod is played daily by a small diehard  community. Servers are paid for and maintained by a small fraction of that community and the servers are constantly being updated with new map rotations and fun ideas. It's amazing what a free mod, for a game I comparitively, barely touch, which I have logged near over a thousand hours on, if I were to use my other top played times as a metric, would bring me so much. I've played with some interesting people which I wouldn't have otherwise, I've laughed, I've gotten angry I've had the time of my life in an era where there are almost too many interchangeable matchmade people to care about who you are even interacting with anymore, I could just be cranky and old. So rather than spewing paragraphs praising Half-Life, which would be much deserved of course, I would like to focus your attention over to the modding community for this game.
Speaking ignorantly and purely from the soul, Half-Life is one of the last games to use a real hard edged netcode, better suited to a local area network, the feeling you get from modern games with lots of interpolation is "smooth" and rather rounded more than square, things are quicker to resolve and while it's healthier and necessary for these modern games to function I can't help but feel like something is lost. A bad analogy might be HL1=vinyl record, HL2=mp3 but you can really feel, every tick and every frame as you traverse whatever world you may inhabit at that time.
Whether you are a diehard Counter-Strike surfer, bhopper or kz_ climbing map addict, maybe you are flying through the skies in Earth Special Forces executing sweet anime stuff I know little about, diving through windows dual pistols clutched and firing in Action Half-Life, bunkering someone in Digital Paintball, providing grand strategy for your living breathing human units with epic macro action in the impressive RTS\FPS hybrid Natural Selection, driving the ball downfield in International Online Soccer or finally taking the game seriously and going prone in Frontline Force, sneaking up to the objective near the enemy line or flip the coin and go back to Counter-Strike one of the most tactical mods to grace the engine. These are just unique ways in which your character is figuratively, holding their hand out as they drag it across the tall grass, as the clear skies upon setting out, have turned grey, and you begin to feel the first light raindrops, almost unsure if they're real as the sensation grows more and more, as you trip and fall face f'n first into the pavement. You can feel this game when you play it, and in a well crafted mod this is all carried over to a completely new experience, now you are considering the value of the game engine itself, goldsrc.
I could write many, many, many.... many more dumb words about how Counter-Strike, TFC, Action-Halflife have given so much to me and I did dedicate a portion of this to Action-Halflife the most fun, stylish and action-oriented mod in my opinion, but I want to give a huge shout and plug to Sven Coop, my lord, they have done a lot of work with goldsrc, like I mentioned before I am completely ignorant and have little knowledge of the true workings of the engine but things I have noticed since playing it as a mod for Half-Life originally, would include, the fact it's now completely free and you don't even need Half-Life 1 so it's standalone now, you can run 200 fps in a goldsrc game which I have never witnessed before, and a little secret incase you wanted HL1 solely for the story, you can play the entire Half-Life 1 campaign, (possibly expansions?) in Sven Coop without even owning Half-Life, I mean hot damn, so feel free to use Sven Coop as a demo of sorts, if anything to experience the feel of the game and its physics.
This has all really been related to multiplayer experiences, simply because that takes the cake for me personally, I didn't even drop one word about the amazing selection of Half-Life singleplayer mods, They Hunger being  hugely popular, Wanted being an excellent western mod, USS darkstar being notable personally with other more recent efforts like, Cry of Fear and Paranoia really pushing the engine, Cry of Fear is standalone and free on steam just like Sven Coop, figured I would mention that. If you love Half-Life mods you know I missed a ton of ground but these are good starting points.

I decided to try the new content out, but alas the game is still botched mess, if not in a worse state than at launch.  The game cannot even get past the first mission without a crash to desktop  with some virtual process already running error.  And from what I have gathered this has been going on since the launch of Shen Last Gift about 4 months ago from the earliest speak of it on the interwebs.  So I'm changing my upvote to a downvote and encourage anyone else to do the same.
Quick review
This game just barely clears me giving a thumbs up, BARELY.
Main review
If you liked X-Com EW/EU then your going to love this, basically the same game.  There in lies my main complaint with this game.  Same stuff, minus alot of the cool stuff for EU (Gene Mods and MEC Trooper), from the previous game are here as well.  But, to me looking at the list side by side, this game contain quite a bit less than the first game and is incrediblly short for a xcom game.  I played on vetern and it started slowly till I hit the first few upgrades and it went be so fast I had all the story objectives queued up to accomplish in a matter of 20mins.  The combat way more easier than it was in the first game.  The main thing that got me killed is the new enemies (Codex, Gatekeeper, and Avatar) as I didnt know their ablities which hurt quite a bit.
The combat seems to lean on the cheap side more than difficult side.  The codex and avatar can disable weapons, making you reload with an aoe attack AND Teleport even when hit (Codex make clones dividing HP b/w them each time) AND Teleport at will ANYWHERE which makes cover pointless in fighting them.  The gatekeeper is about the same as the cyberdisc, just cheaper with more AOE and reanimation.  Other than the Faceless, the game is quite easy to beat..  Sadly this takes alot of the charm out of the game for me at least.
Another Complaint I have and this is a complaint with alot of AAA titles is that they are not QAing the games anymore or at least half-assing QA.  They dont seem to test on multiple PC rigs.  The game launched with the SAME engine as EU/EW mind you and it still came in botched, at the time of writing this it is still desync and jerky in cutscenes and dialog, if they would have at least took one month to play on multiple platforms and different computer rigs, hell my computer is a beast of a system and I couldnt watch any of the cutscenes (gotta love Youtube for helping out on that), would have had a smoother launch.  Game companies as of late are becoming more and more lazy, but we still shell out the cash which tells them to keep doing it.
Final Thoughts
If you can get by the no cutscenes this is short and fun game, but not really worth the 60 bucks for it though.  If you see this on sale for less than 20 pick it otherwise wait.
Side thoughts
They Promised Mod Support and what we got were mods, but no support.  The Documentation for modding was more than likely written by a guy as s/he was taking a dump.  Little more than 10 pgs of info on how to mod for the game.  This is why we ended up with the Corgi gun as the first mod for the game.  I planning on modding for this, but took one look at the documentation and said to hell with it.

I'm not usuially a review kind of guy, but this game is something special and deserves a review.
Darkest Dungeon is not a game for those who can't deal with the concept of every single action having a major concequence, either positive or negative, in the big scheme.  This game WILL push you as an individual and at times it will make you question your desicions and morals.  The game itself comes with a warning that it is a game "about finding the best possible outcome of a bad situation".
That being said, I don't regret a minute I've played this game.  I loved the struggle the game puts you through, and the constant threat of a situation going sour keeps you on your toes, even past the initial shock of the game.  I've completed most of the content in the game, but every time I do a new quest it always feels like a brand new experiance.  Thanks to the unique combat system and the randomized dungeons, the game doesn't begin to feel repetitive.
Lots of people have put in negative reviews on the basis that "RNG KILLED MUH PEOPLE", and to an extent they are right.  This game makes you feel very bad about losing characters, and since there is no way to get them back a character who you've built up over the past 10 hours might be subject to dying at any point in time.  It's rough, but that's part of the beauty of Darkest Dungeon.  Very few other games on the market force you into this type of situation, and even fewer prevent save scumming to get them back (yep you read that right, if you lose someone you can't cheat the system).
All together, Darkest Dungeon is absolutely worth the $25 full price, and if you can get it on sale consider yourself lucky.  It's one of my favorite games from recent years and I think it'll stay that way for a long time.

I decided to try the new content out, but alas the game is still botched mess, if not in a worse state than at launch.  The game cannot even get past the first mission without a crash to desktop  with some virtual process already running error.  And from what I have gathered this has been going on since the launch of Shen Last Gift about 4 months ago from the earliest speak of it on the interwebs.  So I'm changing my upvote to a downvote and encourage anyone else to do the same.
Quick review
This game just barely clears me giving a thumbs up, BARELY.
Main review
If you liked X-Com EW/EU then your going to love this, basically the same game.  There in lies my main complaint with this game.  Same stuff, minus alot of the cool stuff for EU (Gene Mods and MEC Trooper), from the previous game are here as well.  But, to me looking at the list side by side, this game contain quite a bit less than the first game and is incrediblly short for a xcom game.  I played on vetern and it started slowly till I hit the first few upgrades and it went be so fast I had all the story objectives queued up to accomplish in a matter of 20mins.  The combat way more easier than it was in the first game.  The main thing that got me killed is the new enemies (Codex, Gatekeeper, and Avatar) as I didnt know their ablities which hurt quite a bit.
The combat seems to lean on the cheap side more than difficult side.  The codex and avatar can disable weapons, making you reload with an aoe attack AND Teleport even when hit (Codex make clones dividing HP b/w them each time) AND Teleport at will ANYWHERE which makes cover pointless in fighting them.  The gatekeeper is about the same as the cyberdisc, just cheaper with more AOE and reanimation.  Other than the Faceless, the game is quite easy to beat..  Sadly this takes alot of the charm out of the game for me at least.
Another Complaint I have and this is a complaint with alot of AAA titles is that they are not QAing the games anymore or at least half-assing QA.  They dont seem to test on multiple PC rigs.  The game launched with the SAME engine as EU/EW mind you and it still came in botched, at the time of writing this it is still desync and jerky in cutscenes and dialog, if they would have at least took one month to play on multiple platforms and different computer rigs, hell my computer is a beast of a system and I couldnt watch any of the cutscenes (gotta love Youtube for helping out on that), would have had a smoother launch.  Game companies as of late are becoming more and more lazy, but we still shell out the cash which tells them to keep doing it.
Final Thoughts
If you can get by the no cutscenes this is short and fun game, but not really worth the 60 bucks for it though.  If you see this on sale for less than 20 pick it otherwise wait.
Side thoughts
They Promised Mod Support and what we got were mods, but no support.  The Documentation for modding was more than likely written by a guy as s/he was taking a dump.  Little more than 10 pgs of info on how to mod for the game.  This is why we ended up with the Corgi gun as the first mod for the game.  I planning on modding for this, but took one look at the documentation and said to hell with it.

I'm not usuially a review kind of guy, but this game is something special and deserves a review.
Darkest Dungeon is not a game for those who can't deal with the concept of every single action having a major concequence, either positive or negative, in the big scheme.  This game WILL push you as an individual and at times it will make you question your desicions and morals.  The game itself comes with a warning that it is a game "about finding the best possible outcome of a bad situation".
That being said, I don't regret a minute I've played this game.  I loved the struggle the game puts you through, and the constant threat of a situation going sour keeps you on your toes, even past the initial shock of the game.  I've completed most of the content in the game, but every time I do a new quest it always feels like a brand new experiance.  Thanks to the unique combat system and the randomized dungeons, the game doesn't begin to feel repetitive.
Lots of people have put in negative reviews on the basis that "RNG KILLED MUH PEOPLE", and to an extent they are right.  This game makes you feel very bad about losing characters, and since there is no way to get them back a character who you've built up over the past 10 hours might be subject to dying at any point in time.  It's rough, but that's part of the beauty of Darkest Dungeon.  Very few other games on the market force you into this type of situation, and even fewer prevent save scumming to get them back (yep you read that right, if you lose someone you can't cheat the system).
All together, Darkest Dungeon is absolutely worth the $25 full price, and if you can get it on sale consider yourself lucky.  It's one of my favorite games from recent years and I think it'll stay that way for a long time.

Positives
---------------------------------------
Black Squad is a game that has potential to become one of the better if not top f2p online fps games similar to Soldier Front 2 and Arctic Warfare...both of which no longer exist in NA. The game has multiple modes such as TDM, 8v8, and 5v5 to name a few, however this game is played mostly for the competitive 5v5 mode. Black Squad is one of the few games that has very balanced guns with the exception of a few guns of minor superiority. How is this game NOT pay2win? Well sure, there is a cash shop for "bullet" currency that gives you the opportunity to get a head start on the premium weapons as well as skins for the standard guns. HOWEVER! All the premium guns can be bought by "medal" currency which is generously given to you for, Leveling up, Daily Missions and Weekly missions making it possible to get your first premium gun such as the SR47, AK12 or 47, MDR, or the MPX by level 11 at least. The premium guns are however, harder to control and are no way similar to the superiority of the AK and M4 in CSGO. This game has(d) a fairly decent following and competitive scene in Korea as well as Indonesia and I highly recommend watching some videos of their matches to get an idea of how high the skill cap is for Black Squad as the game can be very unforgiving similar to CSGO.
Negatives (CAN BE A HUGE TURN OFF FOR SOME)
---------------------------------------
2 Words ->Toxic Community
It pains me to say this, but this game suffers from some of the WORST toxicity I've ever encountered in a f2p online fps game...which is a shame because this may infact turn off a lot of players due to how prevalent it is especially in 5v5 matches. There really should be no reason for people to be so toxic, but...we all know that 95% of the online fps community is filled with 12-17 year old kids living in their parents home who get bullied at school for being a loser and want to take it out on everyone they meet in a video game...sorry not sorry. Obviously the best thing to do is to ignore them, but I apologize that ANYONE has to deal with this spoiled bahavior as it can create discomfort and lessen your enjoyment of this otherwise great game!
Side note!
---------------------------------------
Hackers may or may not exist, but for the most part I have not had any problems with said "hackers" and more so find that most of my deaths are from making mistakes or getting unlucky so...take this as you will, but try to take the assumption that you need to improve and that the players are better than you rather than call them hackers and defeat yourself. The worst that can happen if you try regardless is that you'll lose that one match, but still improve in some way.

It is about freaking time I type down a review for this game since I've got a hell lot of experience from it.
+ The game story line is that you're one of the species known as "knight's" and your mothership crashed on a rather hostile planet called Cradle. Your main quest is to find energy source big enough to repair the mothership and return to your home planet. I wont say anything more since it could be as a spoiler. The story line is not bad in my opinion. It's good enough to keep you entertained when you are here for the plot.
- The bad part about all of this is that you NEED to upgrade your equipement to progress in the story line. Without getting a "certificate" you cannot proceed with main missions-- which are basically running through dungeon maps killing everything in sight.
+ The graphic aspect somehow keeps up with the nowadays standards of "candy-like" or "cartoony-like" games. Every color is mixed prety well with the background theme of the levels you are going through and even the enemies which stands off from it could make you think how did they got themself's in this perticular area.
- I can not think of anything negative here except of a bit old style and way the polygons are made.
+ Lest talk about the gameplay. It's easy and old school. After you're done with creating your personal knight you being your journey in a tutorial level at the surface that explains you the basics of movement and combat system. For the combat system it brings back stats like piercing and elemental attacks which means you wont kill everything with one kind of weapon. I mean you will but it will take a bit more time to "ages". Various enemies are more resistant to one element or another. The same goes for us where your resistance is described in your armor or in your shield.
- However when you get to the final weapons you need only two kind of weapons to make your way through every level of the game. The most common combination is Dark and Light elemental weapons-- they'll slice or shoot your way through 90% of the foes.
+ You can customize your knight in various ways. Later on if you are rich enough you can change things like your personal color, your eye shape and slightly change your knight's height. Every armor and helmet you can wear as equipement could be set as a "costume" giving you a chance to create your very unique knight. The game offers also "accessories" which are various things you can attach to your helmets and armor freely but it costs quite a lot to later take them off-- so chose wise what to attach.
- I think since two years from now on this game become literally a "fashion simulator" with every update being usually recolors of the most known basic armors tagged as "costume armor" because the developers dont have enough money to make new things or either they run out of ideas.
- if you want to create a perfect and fashionite custom set prepare for A LOT of grinding.
+ Let's talk about music because there's quite a bunch soundtracks here and there. The music is quite good and it really fits the level theme in my opinion. What I'm saying is that if you enter a level which is basically forests, bushes and wolves the theme you'll hear there is jungle-cartoon-like theme which fits perfectly in my opinion.
+ There are basically two high tensioned boss themes. One of them is usually used for arena encounters which is cool and makes the game more dynamic. The second one is the boss theme for all bosses and in my opinion it's the most awesome soundtrack of the whole game where it fits boss fights. Just listen to it- it really matches the tension.
+ One of the biggest pluses here is the community that plays this game. Why is that? Most people that are playing this game are really friendly and they usually help newcomers to understand things around and if you're trying to figure out things and plot-holes in games there are literally tons of these kind of people talking here and there.
- Unfortunatelly the most part of the community probably spends their time playing with their friends or guildmates or even spend time in a closed from public guild hall making fun with people which they know.
- The second con is that this game is slowly decaying because of players that are leaving the game because of the lack of content and to much recolors throwed in our faces.
* In overall I would and I will recommend this game to be played with your friends because it's a lot more enjoyable to play with them rather than playing alone and this game was meant to make friends by meeting strangers-- but right now it is quite hard to manage that.
* However if you like customization and fashion-like games you could give it a try because it has a lot of accessories which unfortunately are somewhat expensive to get from the Auction House.
* If you really like to discover plot of games then you can give a try too! Why? I really dont want to spoil anything but I find the story medicore in terms of nowadays games but it's quite enjoyable as you can think of plenty of theories while getting through it.
I wish you best luck OOO because all you need to do is focus your inner strenght for the ingame content called "story line" and add more events that would bring back old players and add new ones to your community.
Till next time,
have a good day!

It is about freaking time I type down a review for this game since I've got a hell lot of experience from it.
+ The game story line is that you're one of the species known as "knight's" and your mothership crashed on a rather hostile planet called Cradle. Your main quest is to find energy source big enough to repair the mothership and return to your home planet. I wont say anything more since it could be as a spoiler. The story line is not bad in my opinion. It's good enough to keep you entertained when you are here for the plot.
- The bad part about all of this is that you NEED to upgrade your equipement to progress in the story line. Without getting a "certificate" you cannot proceed with main missions-- which are basically running through dungeon maps killing everything in sight.
+ The graphic aspect somehow keeps up with the nowadays standards of "candy-like" or "cartoony-like" games. Every color is mixed prety well with the background theme of the levels you are going through and even the enemies which stands off from it could make you think how did they got themself's in this perticular area.
- I can not think of anything negative here except of a bit old style and way the polygons are made.
+ Lest talk about the gameplay. It's easy and old school. After you're done with creating your personal knight you being your journey in a tutorial level at the surface that explains you the basics of movement and combat system. For the combat system it brings back stats like piercing and elemental attacks which means you wont kill everything with one kind of weapon. I mean you will but it will take a bit more time to "ages". Various enemies are more resistant to one element or another. The same goes for us where your resistance is described in your armor or in your shield.
- However when you get to the final weapons you need only two kind of weapons to make your way through every level of the game. The most common combination is Dark and Light elemental weapons-- they'll slice or shoot your way through 90% of the foes.
+ You can customize your knight in various ways. Later on if you are rich enough you can change things like your personal color, your eye shape and slightly change your knight's height. Every armor and helmet you can wear as equipement could be set as a "costume" giving you a chance to create your very unique knight. The game offers also "accessories" which are various things you can attach to your helmets and armor freely but it costs quite a lot to later take them off-- so chose wise what to attach.
- I think since two years from now on this game become literally a "fashion simulator" with every update being usually recolors of the most known basic armors tagged as "costume armor" because the developers dont have enough money to make new things or either they run out of ideas.
- if you want to create a perfect and fashionite custom set prepare for A LOT of grinding.
+ Let's talk about music because there's quite a bunch soundtracks here and there. The music is quite good and it really fits the level theme in my opinion. What I'm saying is that if you enter a level which is basically forests, bushes and wolves the theme you'll hear there is jungle-cartoon-like theme which fits perfectly in my opinion.
+ There are basically two high tensioned boss themes. One of them is usually used for arena encounters which is cool and makes the game more dynamic. The second one is the boss theme for all bosses and in my opinion it's the most awesome soundtrack of the whole game where it fits boss fights. Just listen to it- it really matches the tension.
+ One of the biggest pluses here is the community that plays this game. Why is that? Most people that are playing this game are really friendly and they usually help newcomers to understand things around and if you're trying to figure out things and plot-holes in games there are literally tons of these kind of people talking here and there.
- Unfortunatelly the most part of the community probably spends their time playing with their friends or guildmates or even spend time in a closed from public guild hall making fun with people which they know.
- The second con is that this game is slowly decaying because of players that are leaving the game because of the lack of content and to much recolors throwed in our faces.
* In overall I would and I will recommend this game to be played with your friends because it's a lot more enjoyable to play with them rather than playing alone and this game was meant to make friends by meeting strangers-- but right now it is quite hard to manage that.
* However if you like customization and fashion-like games you could give it a try because it has a lot of accessories which unfortunately are somewhat expensive to get from the Auction House.
* If you really like to discover plot of games then you can give a try too! Why? I really dont want to spoil anything but I find the story medicore in terms of nowadays games but it's quite enjoyable as you can think of plenty of theories while getting through it.
I wish you best luck OOO because all you need to do is focus your inner strenght for the ingame content called "story line" and add more events that would bring back old players and add new ones to your community.
Till next time,

I managed to get my squad over to the building and to the VIP, all while maintaining my concealment. Oddly enough, your turns still tick down when you are concealed, but why is that? What reason do we have to rush when the enemy have no idea we are even there?
So, I have my squad all positioned in the building and proceed to hack the door to release the VIP. Little did I know that hacking that door would alert the entire map, which consisted of around 10 enemies, with at least 4 or 5 Vipers (oh boy) So, the enemies rush in, the majority of my squad miss their Overwatch shots (no surprises there) and of course, we are surrounded. Vipers begin to grab team members and pull them away, another Viper spits at 2 squad members and those Codex enemies begin to disable my weapons, Teleport and Clone whenever being damaged. And don't forget, the turn timer is ticking down while this chaos is happening.
Then it gets even worse as reinforcements are on the way. Now that sounds bad enough, but it turns out they are dropping in right next to the extraction zone. The extraction zone is also right outside of the building we are currently in. Surrounded, weapons disabled, trapped by Vipers, reinforcements covering our escape and only 2-3 turns left. There is absolutely no chance the squad can defend themselves and make it to the extraction in such a short time. Yeah, like hell is anyone making it out alive.
I was enjoying this game when I first began to play it. It felt like an amazing game and I honestly thought the turn timed missions would be a nice addition to the game, but it doesn't take the game long to heavily spike in diFFiculty and not in a good way. I like a challenge in my games, but the insane crap you have to put up with in this game makes what should be challenging, just a huge annoyance. The timed missions, while they do have potential, honestly seem poorly done to me. It feels like you need the knowledge of what enemy types you will be facing and where the enemies will spawn beforehand, because the timed missions seem so tight that you need that perfect plan, if you want everyone to make it.
Don't get me wrong, the game is great and is in many ways an improvement of the first, but it has quickly become more of an annoyance than fun. So, as much as I want to recommend this game, I just can't.

Maybe Black Mesa... or how Gordon Freeman changed the world - a must-have, if you're not a graphic next-gen purist.
During an experiment gone wrong, where you're the one that pushed the crystal into the analyzer, you're the only hope of the survivors to reach the search and rescue team, because of your combinaison. However, you'll have to survive from the attacks of your coworkers transformed in zombies and creatures coming from another world. And unfortunately for you, your only weapon is a crowbar. And you're just a scientist employed by Black Mesa...
That's Half-Life for you. A scientist relying on a crowbar first before becoming an expert in weapons. The story is perhaps basic and with some twists but noneless, the universe build around Half-Life has expanded a lot.
However, if Half-Life is a FPS, which means weapons to shoot any enemies, that you can carry thanks to your wonderful combinaison, you can find some puzzles throughout the game, mainly because of the need to wander around a destroyed facility.
What's fascinating in Half-Life isn't probably the gameplay in itself. I mean, everything seems very basic. But if it wasn't for it, you wouldn't have mods like Counter-Strike around. I don't know why I was fascinated by Half-Life. I mean, it's not like jumping was new or that weapons were innovative... maybe the iconic crowbar has to do something with. Or maybe it's just that a plot, perhaps basic but very effective, the mysterious G-Man following you around and disappearing easily or that the fact it's someone that wasn't trained to become the hero of the world... or maybe the ending. I don't know but I just know that when I played it, I was fascinated.
I was fascinated by the fact that you can find survivors around that can help you, guards or scientists. Or the fact that some of them meet a tragic fate under your eyes. I was fascinated by the change of the objectives: from reaching the surface, you're now the only hope to end an invasion and the wiping of any survivor by the soldiers.
I don't remember any problem with the gameplay apart the treacherous ladders. Climbing them isn't hard. However, when you needed to step out of them OR going down, it was a challenge. And the famous jumping with the crates where you were sliding...
Half-Life has the graphics from 1998 and it was very good ones. Even now, I could still enjoy them. I don't say that it's detailed. But you can see some interesting details. And Xen, the other world, despite being a challenge, is very beautiful.
Besides, the soundtrack is also great. It's only heard during some important moments. But the music is powerful.
Half-Life is a classic to have. Gordon Freeman is a character that you can't forget.

I'm not sure if it is just bad RNG, but I honestly believe I was on a mission that was impossible to beat whilst keeping my entire squad of 6 members alive. I had 12 turns to get across the map, hack a door to release the VIP and then proceed to escape. That sounds easy in theory, but in practice, boy was I screwed. I managed to get my squad over to the building and to the VIP, all while maintaining my concealment. Oddly enough, your turns still tick down when you are concealed, but why is that? What reason do we have to rush when the enemy have no idea we are even there?
So, I have my squad all positioned in the building and proceed to hack the door to release the VIP. Little did I know that hacking that door would alert the entire map, which consisted of around 10 enemies, with at least 4 or 5 Vipers (oh boy) So, the enemies rush in, the majority of my squad miss their Overwatch shots (no surprises there) and of course, we are surrounded. Vipers begin to grab team members and pull them away, another Viper spits at 2 squad members and those Codex enemies begin to disable my weapons, Teleport and Clone whenever being damaged. And don't forget, the turn timer is ticking down while this chaos is happening.
Then it gets even worse as reinforcements are on the way. Now that sounds bad enough, but it turns out they are dropping in right next to the extraction zone. The extraction zone is also right outside of the building we are currently in. Surrounded, weapons disabled, trapped by Vipers, reinforcements covering our escape and only 2-3 turns left. There is absolutely no chance the squad can defend themselves and make it to the extraction in such a short time. Yeah, like hell is anyone making it out alive.
I was enjoying this game when I first began to play it. It felt like an amazing game and I honestly thought the turn timed missions would be a nice addition to the game, but it doesn't take the game long to heavily spike in diFFiculty and not in a good way. I like a challenge in my games, but the insane crap you have to put up with in this game makes what should be challenging, just a huge annoyance. The timed missions, while they do have potential, honestly seem poorly done to me. It feels like you need the knowledge of what enemy types you will be facing and where the enemies will spawn beforehand, because the timed missions seem so tight that you need that perfect plan, if you want everyone to make it.
Don't get me wrong, the game is great and is in many ways an improvement of the first, but it has quickly become more of an annoyance than fun. So, as much as I want to recommend this game, I just can't.

This game is fantastic!
Okay. I know what you're thinking: This game is a ripoff of Terraria.
Well, to answer that, I will say yes. Partially. This game, in my opinion, is vastly superior to Terraria. Where Terraria is only one world that you can explore, This one is several billions, probably. This game also has tons of recipes, which makes it way more awesome. Take Minecraft, for instance. The gameplay is good, it is fun. However, you get tired of it quite fast. You're either going to go out of things to craft, redstone contraptions to make, or building ideas. That's not the case here! There are a ton of solar systems to explore, there are plenty of recipes to craft. There is also quite a few nifty machines to use.
Now, let's summarize the pros and cons of this game.
Pros:
- Amazing soundtrack
- Tons of stuff to do
- Good interface
- Good story
Cons:
- The navigation system could have been a little better, for instance: you get more info about the planet that you're landing on.
- Too high fuel consumption when going from planet to planet.
- Could have been a little more RPG-ish: Communicate with NPCs, make alliances, make like a "single player community"
- Denser ores. The ore system just doesn't feel right. I feel that it should have had different levels, so that for instance: diamonds can only be found in deep places. Right now, you can find diamond on the surface.
- More to the space element: Add more in the space-area. Maybe some black holes, some supernovas here and there, and some antimatter/dark matter couldn't hurt.
- Gravity changes. On planets with more mass, you are heavier, and therefore slower, don't jump quite as high, etc.
Overall, the cons were more suggestions than cons, so this game still deserves a 5/5. Also, take to consideration that it is in beta.

My Review
I think I have enough time in to give a decent review--although I will mention as more mods released I found myself restarting the game multiple times. Most mods as of yet are relatively simple---guns, armor, more classes, longer timers, no timers, no alien move when spotted, etc etc. The modding abilities in the game would allow complete reworks well beyond what Long War managed and all we need here is time--but as of now there's not really much in the way of reworking the game and gameplay. For this review about all I've ended up using is timer tweaks and some gun and armor mods for more customization. Cheat mods are out-but quite frankly I see little use for them because compared to EW the A.I. is rather simple --In EW when you upped the difficulty that included extra A.I. routines to both tactics and patrol, as well as aim, hitpoint and other bonus's. Here I've seen nothing A.I. wise on the most difficult level--and I'm actually pretty close to finishing the game on that difficulty and have yet suffered a squaddie death other than the two canned deaths in the tutorial.

The setting
By now most know this sequel's overall story starts with the Alien's win, man's agreement with/for Advent and your basically an underground resistance group. We have to assume here somewhere after the first game's completion and this game there was another wave incoming the 1st game was unaware of. I can suspend my disbelief enough to accept that basic premise but unfortunately Firaxis fails to carry this to logical conclusions. I can't expand on this without going into spoilers so be prepared for them--because this needs to be said ---as STORY is a huge part driving the game.
At first I liked the idea. XCOM was conquered, the council wanted to surrender. The aliens had total ground and air superiority. And here you are--Mr. French resistance trying to fight back, expose the real truth (Matrix style), and defeat the BIG LIE and Advent. But as the story goes on and more is learned about the Aliens real motivations you simply left scratching your head.
So why form the Advent Coalition at all? If the only thing they want humans for is raw material put them in stasis at will! Why spend vast amount of resources creating giant gleaming cities and a global infrastructure to maintain them if you're just going to kill them all for some DNA juice?
It would've been far more interesting to me if the aliens had a different motive. As it is they are as shallow as Exalt.
Your Base
your basically set up like in EU except your a ship that flies around the globe making contact with the resistance. Once done you get a default retaliation mission that mirrors terror missions in EU. Other random missions include supply, intel, recruits. Some expose Advent targets. The DOOM timer grows and mostly your gathering resources to open a region to reduce said timer. Repeat and rinse. About all we had for base attack/defend in the first game was a single mission in EW. Here an alien ship flies around trying to spot you, and you get shot down and the base attacked...but it's ultimately a huge letdown as all combat occurs on an ouside map and all one needs to do is destroy a beacon and return to the ship platform. Overall, timers or not-all missions have a sameness although the on the fly maps are an overall improvment to the canned maps of EU. There's no going into saucer missions as in EU...and you WILL MISS THEM. Although there are missions involving saucers--don't get your hopes up.

Overall the missions lack both the OOOMPH! and the difficulty of the first game. I cannot rate mission options very high here at all. None are really interesting and the most difficult ones aren't difficult because of structure or layout but usually because of gamey placements of the enemy and thier over-the-top ability bonus's. As an example you have to destroy some device the game spawns enemies pretty much in the same room and sorrounding area. Worse, devices you need to defend see the same spawns on top of the device. Add in mission timers and every mission is about belining to the spot before the timer expires.

Poor excuse for timers
As I mentioned before mission briefing rarely justify the timers and the overall DOOM advent timer rushes one through the game. Easily modded out but as it stands this was just a horrible idea. If you think it ADDS hard choices, your just nuts. It ADDS nothing. Timers or not all missions are the same. It does take away quite a bit and a lot more than simply turtling on overwatch. You lack the time to strategically move your team where you might want them to come into the target. All in all your one and only choice is to get the job done before said timer expires or stop said timer-and there's just one strategy for that. Straight out of tinkertown web gaming or The land of Concoles to use these designs in a game like this is like removing the cheese from a cheesburger. The person who thought them up can't be slapped enough, and if he goes down a couple more kicks is highly warranted.

The Geoscape of Interruption
That's it's new name and it's perfectly fitting. First, the whole idea of having to scan everything to get something done is fine in itself--though logically it's just a gamey way for replacing scanning for alien ships in EU-and that's pretty much it--you Scan to get things done, be it make contact, get supplies, get recruits and of course get a headache---because each and every scan--be it 3 days or 6 days, will get interrupted multiple times. Research is complete, item manufactures, room buult, scientist farted, whatever--the flow of this is about as disconcerting and jolting as it can be, and even with nearly 70 hrs in I just can't get used to it. There needs to be a mod addressing the flow here so things go much more fluid and logically. Hell, illogically as long as the interruptions stop. Worse you can't get an overall view because the damn Geoscape does not zoom out to where you can see the whole globe--dispite it looking just like that in the control room.

Mighty Morphing Power Ranger Music
You hear it going into and exiting missions...and it just does not fit the XCOM universe. The original played like a horror game--with music that fit the ANTISIPATION of what might pop out next. Even EU had better. Now, once on the mission there's a nice ambient thump thump thump background music that reminds me of John Carpenter's The Thing---I like that--but any mod that does away with the Jackie Chan crap is being immediately downloaded by me.

In Need of Balancing
Swords are neat...early. They're useless later. You will find armor, weapons and soldier perks are not very well balanced at all.Mods to the resue.
But my biggiest complaint overall is the A.I. Half the time it doesn't take cover on advancing-and most times the way it advances is an easy Turkey Shoot. In fact the current A.I. improvment mod that is out does just that- prevents the A.I. from advancing---or in other words--stops the A.I. routines from executing---because what's there is so horrible. I'm not kidding-go read the mod's discription and it flat it tells you it's doing just that and all the over the top alien abilities can't hide it.
Underwhelming amount of content and paid mods again.

This game is fantastic!
Okay. I know what you're thinking: This game is a ripoff of Terraria.
Well, to answer that, I will say yes. Partially. This game, in my opinion, is vastly superior to Terraria. Where Terraria is only one world that you can explore, This one is several billions, probably. This game also has tons of recipes, which makes it way more awesome. Take Minecraft, for instance. The gameplay is good, it is fun. However, you get tired of it quite fast. You're either going to go out of things to craft, redstone contraptions to make, or building ideas. That's not the case here! There are a ton of solar systems to explore, there are plenty of recipes to craft. There is also quite a few nifty machines to use.
Now, let's summarize the pros and cons of this game.
Pros:
- Amazing soundtrack
- Tons of stuff to do
- Good interface
- Good story
Cons:
- The navigation system could have been a little better, for instance: you get more info about the planet that you're landing on.
- Too high fuel consumption when going from planet to planet.
- Could have been a little more RPG-ish: Communicate with NPCs, make alliances, make like a "single player community"
- Denser ores. The ore system just doesn't feel right. I feel that it should have had different levels, so that for instance: diamonds can only be found in deep places. Right now, you can find diamond on the surface.
- More to the space element: Add more in the space-area. Maybe some black holes, some supernovas here and there, and some antimatter/dark matter couldn't hurt.
- Gravity changes. On planets with more mass, you are heavier, and therefore slower, don't jump quite as high, etc.
Overall, the cons were more suggestions than cons, so this game still deserves a 5/5. Also, take to consideration that it is in beta.

An excellent sequel for an excellent game. The new game mechanics are a nice touch, the game has a different approach to the old game, but is familiar enough for those who love the XCOM: Enemy unknown/Enemy within. I enjoy playing it a lot, even though it annoys me like all XCOM-games. 91% hit chance... yeah right, more like 50%. But that's not really too bad.
POSSIBLE SPOILER ALERT FROM HERE ON!
But one thing annoys me beyond reason. In the new missions there is a serious flaw in mission design. A huge bunch of missions demand, that the player must complete at least one part of the mission in something like 8 rounds. A bomb goes off or whatever.
At first it seemed like a nice touch wich upped the tempo of the game. But the further I have come in the came, the more it annoys me, like you wouldn't believe. You have to run towards your goal with almost no regard for cover so the concealment factor of the game is almost completely useless. And with the hit propabilities which didn't annoy at first became a real pain the♥♥♥♥♥♥ when you realize that you almost always are left with just 1 or 2 rounds to go and having alerted the whole friggin' map of your presence.
This has made me feel that I have to take 1 rookie to every damn mission and just send him in to a certain death just to get the bloody timer off. This is in my opinion a really bad flaw to the game. Maybe I'm not that good at playing the game, or maybe I need to sharpen my tactics, but as it extremely often happens that my guys miss their shots with decent hit propabilities or only hit very lightly and the enemy just mows down my units I rarely feel that I can get to my objective in time.
But even with this terrible flaw, the game has potential, feels fresh but familiar and mostly I am enjoying playing it. Will start again with a different tactic in mind and see where it takes me.

This title is wholly recommended, especially towards sandbox-construction and Action RPG fans. A list of various features is as follows for an easier read. Review was revised for 09/2017.
-A procedurally-generated, voxel-based MMO created by Trion Games. Has the visual appeal similar to Skysaga/ Minecraft, and focuses primarily on acquiring items from dungeons.
-The core flow of the game is to repeatedly raid Dungeons and Lairs to acquire better hats, face-masks and weapons to equip on the given character, while depositing older equipment specifically for visual customization. Loot given is always for the currently chosen Class.
-Uses a ‘Master Rank’ system to let the player know how much time has been invested on their given account, at a glance. There are bonuses applied to a given account for each rank up (for example: Master Rank 5 unlocks the Trading Post and Community Chest, as well as increasing the Elysian Flask usage by 1).
-PVP released on November 17th, 2015. It currently has Capture The Flag and Team Deathmatch. Matches are 3v3 or 5v5.
-When the player first starts, they go through a brief Tutorial instance with their first chosen Class, before being dropped into the Hub World proper.
-As of this writing, the game was having consistent latency issues and crashes due to Trion Games having reached their current database server limit across all of their given titles. This resulted in a lot of negative criticism from fans; the company was planning to implement a database server upgrade by the end of November 2015, and has been resolved. It is speculated that the Xbox One and PS4 version releases were being used as a distraction while the PC issue was being addressed.
Tips:
-All Classes can be bought from the Shop using Credits, which are exclusively the in-game Shop currencies, or from the Chaos Crafter table. Credits (rainbow-coloured Cubits; paid in-game Shop currency) are only acquired by purchasing it from the Shop or as a Mastery Rank reward. Don’t worry about the prices- they tend to be fairly low during promotions, such as Halloween. By using a Class Coin, a player can instantaneously unlock a Class of their choosing.
-The Refer-a-Friend code feature is used as an incentive for older players (Master Rank 50+) to help newer players level up to at least Master Rank 20. Upon entering the code, the receiver earns a free Class Coin, while the giver only gets their reward once the receiver hits Master Rank 20. There are reward increments for the giver at their 1st, 3rd, 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, and 30th recruit that reaches Master Rank 20 (Elder Dragon mount line).
-Every Class hits a level maximum of Lv30. Lv1-10 is often considered to be the game’s tutorial instances (Novice for Lv1-3, Adept for 4/ 5, Elite for 6/ 7, and Master for 8/ 9). Lv10 and up contains 9 separate Uber instances. Players originally had to craft the Uber 2 through 6 portals to advance after reaching Lv12 for a given Class, but the entire progression was reworked under a Power Rank system commonly seen amongst mobile MMOs.
-Equipment can be used to boost a Classes’ level from 21-42; the Gear level, as it’s called, maxes out at Lv22. This essentially means either upgrading existing gear, swapping gear out for better drops, or grinding Shadow Towers. For example, a simple 0-Star, Shadow Level 1 being upgraded to a 3-Star, Shadow Level 2 piece of equipment boosts a Class by 1 level. No longer relevant due to the new Power Rank system and progression.
-It is common for players to have a ‘main’ Class (used most often), and at least one ‘secondary’ Class. Most veteran players typically have at least 4 or 5 XP-maxed Classes, with one or two having reached the overall cap of Lv42.
-There are mounts, and then there are Dragon Ascension mounts. These dragons are acquired by crafting and consuming their respective Dragon Souls. They all start off at 0, but at 10 the Fledgling mount is unlocked; 50 unlocks the Adult mount; 100 unlocks the Ascended mount, which can spit explosive projectiles. Don’t be surprised if the majority of mounts seen are Dragon mounts- they appear to outclass normal mounts because of their unique gliding ability.
-Once a player reaches Mastery Rank 20, Challenges are unlocked. These consist of the following:
Dungeon Raid: Raiding dungeons/ lairs of a specific biome, with a 20 minute time limit. Two classes will be picked randomly as bonus classes, which grant the player more points per quest clear.
Race Challenge: A gliding Time Trial in its own instance.
Coin Challenge: Coin Collection within a 1:30 time limit, in its own instance.
-Players commonly call each other’s progress by instance or Master Rank (“[player] is Master Rank 10.” or “I’m only on the Master instance at the moment.”). Don’t be surprised to see players not bother with Uber 4-6 until they hit level 25 or higher.
-There are ‘Golden Thread’ Quests given in order, that range from beginner tasks all the way up to end-game tasks, in order to ease newer players into the game.
-The Elysian Flask is a players only means of healing immediately, so use it sparingly! Natural HP regeneration is fine, and can be boosted with equipment, but it’s recommended to replenish it after clearing a few Dungeons or after clearing a single Lair.
-The Badge feature is used to like an Achievement system of sorts- except upon meeting the criteria for the award, the player is instantly given a set amount of Mastery points.
-Oftentimes, the player will want to consider which type of damage a given Class uses. For example, the Lunar Lancer Class uses a Lance, thus dealing physical damage; the Gunslinger Class uses dual Laser Pistols, which would imply physical damage, but it is actually magic damage. The same goes for Bows- they deal physical damage, but it is implied that they deal Magic instead.
-The ‘Lasermancy’ statistic is used for building/ destroying blocks in Build Mode.
-The ‘Magic Find’ statistic builds up with each consecutive quest cleared without dying. When it reaches an increment of 10, it activates, upgrading the tier of rewards for the player. It has a cap, however.
-Unwanted equipment should be deposited first in the ‘Loot Depositor’ table, thus adding it to a player’s given collection- then if they get a duplicate, it can be deposited for additional materials. Each style that is deposited for the first time grants the player a single Mastery Point.
-For every 100th Mastery Point accumulated, the overall Mastery Rank increases by 1. There are some great bonuses to be had starting from Mastery Rank 30, and the maximum is 300. The downside means grinding loot, especially once all of the Classes have been unlocked, and have reached their maximum. With 4 Classes, a player can comfortably reach and surpass Mastery Rank 50.

Ok, this is the only review for any games i've done but I think this game deserves it. Unturned is easily my favorite game in my steam library. I've seen it go through to many stages and highly reccomend it. What you may pass off as "just another zombie survival" is actually a great game that I would reccomend to everyone. A lot of people like to compare it to Minecraft because of the graphics. While this may be true that the graphics look alike, Unturned has so much more to offer the Minecraft (Not saying that Minecaft is bad or anything just saying that the comparison is a bit bad) and not just guns. Unurned has a better storage, loot, base, eating/drinking and many, many more things. Also, the maps in this game are not ramdomly generated and are completely handcrafted. From Washington to Germany to Alpha Valley, the maps are very fun to play and have a natural feel of flow to them. I have only 2 complaints about Unturned and they are very acceptable. 1) When playing on singleplayer I occasionaly get a weird bug that I am not allowed to leave the game unless I open the devkit or use my computer's task managers, and both of those ways do not save and it gets really annoying when I get really lucky and get good loot only to have it all go away, but this is most likely because of my computer's crappyness. 2) The servers in this game are divided into 2 sections. Regular and Gold. Regular servers are able to be joined from the start of the game while gold servers are part of a "DLC" part of the game that costs $20 and gives you a bunch of cosmetic items and the ability to join gold servers. I think this is ok because this game is created by one person and the purchase of gold supports him tremendously. Overall, I would reccomend this game to anyone and everyone. This game alone is enough to make the year 2016 an awesome PC gaming year. What an amazing turn-based strategy game, with a staggering amount of nice character customization (especially with Steam Workshop mods). If you liked XCOM: Enemy Unknown, you will like this even more. If you never played the first one, you will still like this one. With a full mod support from the moment of release, and with the SDK now available, the game will have an extremely high replay value. We already have tons of great mod content, and its only getting better. Highly recommended to any and all friends of turn-based strategy games! If I believed in numeric ranking, this would be a solid 9/10.
Why not 10/10? My personal complaints:
- The game has some serious performance problems: with i7-3770k, 16GB RAM, GTX 970 and played from a 250GB Samsung EVO 850 SSD, @1440p or @1080p and medium/high settings (won't matter much), the game will average to about 35-50fps, will constantly drop below 25fps, sometimes even below 15fps(!). Lowering quality and/or resolution won't help much, so the problem is deep in the game. Holding steady 60fps is very rare.  This must be fixed ASAP! Starbound is a very interesting - and I would even venture to say innovative - game. It's a sandbox game like Minecraft, with 2D roots from Terraria. What makes it innovative? A number of things.
For starters, Starbound isn't just pseudo-fantasy themed like either of the formers. It's space. The final frontier, some would say, and a vast one at that. Granted, the worlds being randomly generated from what is in the game so far leave something to be desired, but take it with a grain of salt. It is early beta, after all. (Besides, space faction battles anyone?)
The pixelated art style is by no means innovative, but the dynamic lighting and organic animation adds a nice flare to the 8-bit art. That, combined with the atmosphere (or lack thereof) of space and awe-inspiring music keeps pulling my attention.
Another aspect that sets Starbound apart from the others is the lore. It might not be apparent at the surface, but Starbound has a story to tell and a decent-sized cast of characters. This isn't just humans trekking through the stars (though they certainly exist here), but other races as well with different governments and the likes.
The Apex are an ape-like species being supressed by a 1984-style totalitarianism. Florans, who, although primitive plant creatures, are very fierce. The Hylotl are rather silly, essentially being Japanese fish (koi?), yet still very attractive. Avians are bird people (kinda like Falco from Star Fox) with a mayan-esque culture. Then there are Glitches, who are robotic people with a medieval flare. And finally there is the Novakid, which are beings of light with a taste for cowboy hats?
Okay, so the lore is a little bit cartoon-ish, but it's still very interesting and worth a read.
Now, the game is still deep in the development cycle, so there are a lot of features that will change as the game improves, but it is entirely playable as is and will probably devour hours upon hours of you and your friends' free time. But, do take this word of advice, and be mindful of meteor showers. :)

I'm actually surprised how much I liked this game as I totally overplayed the original. I played it so much that I'm part of the half percent that got the 'complete the game on every continent' achievement.
I hate how the story actually ret cons my play experience assuming I failed, and I initially was sour grapes enough to not buy the game. After the positive reviews, I decided to just grab it and support an awesome company and develper.
The story is great. It feels like the series 'V' over the 'Independence Day' feel of the original game.Being essentially a terrorist of the aliens gives the game a totally unique feel.
The different classes are mostly all very compelling. In this game I had a tougher time choosing the perfect squad (2 snipers and no heavy? 1 of each class? 2 assault classes?) .
Managing the building in the base is simplified yet makes much more of an impact based on your choices. The formula and balancing of each building choice really makes more of an impact despeite having fewer squares than the original.
The Doomsday clock is NOT overwhelming and 'rush-rush' like most people fear. It only gives the game a better balance adding a parameter to keep players from grinding and over boosting their funds.
I lost the first game completely and whined. But, after 10 hours and a retry (on iron mode nevertheless) I wasn't able to put the game down. The beginning game is much harder before getting the upgrades to the armor and weapons. So hang in there, Tiger!
The main map can become annoying because everything takes a few days to do and missions interrupt the flow of your concentration. I actually like this, it really trains my brain to multitask! It's very much like running an important opperation in real life. If you can't handle it, write out notes on a piece of paper to get your mind organized on the long, short and medium range goals.
Every enemy is quite unique, and they are NOT just reskins of the last game. It becomes a hard decision to know which enemy angers us most. I still vote for the Codex!
I'm not super huge into customization of my soldiers, but I love the implementation this time around with the character pool option. I found it really silly in the first game to customize a soldier after having a template already made up. It felt like I was doing bizaar operations rather than actual customization. Now you can prebuild the characters and have them randomly show up in the main game as recruits for hire. This is the first game that I actually too advantage of the modding community (I know, I'm NOOB casual pc gamer scum). I am shocked at how well the mods meld (xcom 1 reference intended) with the actual game! This just opened up Pandora's box for my mind. I do reccomend some of the UI mods to further improve the game.
I did have annoying glitches and a couple of crashes. Believe me, they are tedious when the game makes the stakes so high. Sometimes, I cannot find the last enemy and they seemed to have teleported or they actually were pretty much hidden or off the map. It's not too aggregious, but they do pop up. The worst was my first game finish. The final battle had basically no graphics and white blotches everywhere. These glitches sometimes affect only one crew member. Even a save and reload won't help. So, there will be no animations for just my specialist but all the other people are fine. The loading times and drame rates are ridiculous. Even what I thought were prerendered cut scenes seme to chug along. The actual battlefield is ok, but the stuff between the base management and the battles are crazy. I am running a rig with 16 gigs of ram, gtx 980 and an SSD for reference. I am well above the recommended specs in all categories. So, I hope there is better optimization in the future.
The base management, resource management seem to take on a way more important role. I actually find it very fun despite less time on the battlefield.  I think the new characters are pretty lame and social justice warriory but not obnoxiously so. I totally would get this game again and just warn people to put at least 10 hours into it before getting the flow of the new changes.
I wont spoil the upgrade and research system, but I find it refreshing and superior to the original. This team really did give something special. This to me is The Dark Knight or Terminator 2. It's a sequel that takes a great property and vastly improves upon it.
Mindboggling fun, I don't even know why it's fun, It just is.

I've seen it go through to many stages and highly reccomend it. What you may pass off as "just another zombie survival" is actually a great game that I would reccomend to everyone. A lot of people like to compare it to Minecraft because of the graphics. While this may be true that the graphics look alike, Unturned has so much more to offer the Minecraft (Not saying that Minecaft is bad or anything just saying that the comparison is a bit bad) and not just guns. Unurned has a better storage, loot, base, eating/drinking and many, many more things. Also, the maps in this game are not ramdomly generated and are completely handcrafted. From Washington to Germany to Alpha Valley, the maps are very fun to play and have a natural feel of flow to them. I have only 2 complaints about Unturned and they are very acceptable. 1) When playing on singleplayer I occasionaly get a weird bug that I am not allowed to leave the game unless I open the devkit or use my computer's task managers, and both of those ways do not save and it gets really annoying when I get really lucky and get good loot only to have it all go away, but this is most likely because of my computer's crappyness. 2) The servers in this game are divided into 2 sections. I played all UFO games in the series, starting with the famous original game (hell yeah). Here are my first impressions:
- Graphics is 8-10 years behind the contemporary games: Coarse, disproportional, extremely poor quality for 2016. Consider GTA V for comparison, which is MUCH more detailed in all aspects. And I paid less for GTA.
V. 15 years old (!) Neverwinter Nights feels smoother and cleaner than XCOM2. XCOM2 is a bunch of graphic features that do not mix at all. Moreover, it's the same feeling about the game - it doesn't mix well.
- Comics-based design. That brings a frivolous flavor into the game, it's SO OFF from the original series idea! Splashy-flashy nonesense instead of honed atmosphere of terror. If you try to employ comics-like design for legendary UFO series than something definitely went wrong. It's like if FIFA game would have added barbie girl teams to harvest 10-years old female audience.
- AI. Oh my gosh... These guys introduced timers solely because their AI is umm... non-functional. The whole idea behind the timers is to cover the incapable AI. First group of monsters is coming, second of monsters groups is coming, and so on. Is it 2016, really? Enemies do not employ various tactics (variable group AI was implemented 10 years ago in multiple game titles), yet here monsters just mostly rush. This makes tactical combat identical, only decoration changes. A total, complete fail.
- Linear gameplay, lack of control. Feverish attempts to treat old XCOM gameplay issues just brought more issues and the need for crutches. You are only allowed to obtain certain perks after you play a mission that is palmed off by designers.
- Little things: pauses, idling, poor animations, weird camera angles, bugs with path finding to name a few.
- Swords! Yeah, can't wait for medieval cavalry and trebushets in the next releases. Of course this is easier than create an AI!..
- Weapon modifiers.
- Tactical missions are faster (for a price my friends, for a price...)
- Nice body physics. Too pronounced but at least something stands out of this sad feature collection named "a game".
- Solved "next floor" problem, no need to switch between floors.
- An attempt to improve research and engineering, not bad.
- Great demolishions!
In short, this game looks like a Marvel comics to me. The biggest problem of this game is that it lacks composition integrity, it's plain, confusing, unpolished and sterile. Visually it's more a grotesque rather than an atmospheric game. It a definite downgrade after the first XCOM. No problem, we will wait another 5-10 years until glamour barbie designers/producers are substituted by the folks that understand the genre.
P.S. Frankly, this is one of those rare games I would like to return and get my money back.

XCOM 2 delivers a fast paced fun strategic run. You're constantly under pressure, and all your choises feel momentous. When on the strategic map you're under pressure from Advent's project Avatar that continually advances. You're never granted anything freely. Suply from other resistance cells need to be collected and that takes time, intel needs to be gathered at XCOM HQ and that take time, a number of tasks will be sprinkled around the map that could grant you boni, but they take time, you need to expand your network of resistance cells, but guess what: that takes time.
While you're doing this the Avatar project will advance, missions will spawn that you need to react to, dark events will trigger unless you counter them with a mission, oh and you'll not be able to counter all dark events so bad things will happen and you'll just have to deal.
And that's just on the strategic holomap. On missions you're usually under preassure. Most missions will have a countdown timer until your objective becomes unavaliable, or worse until your extraction window closes and the remaining soldiers are capured and lost. Other missions are like the old terror missions, but the aliens are now targeting resistance havens and you need to extract the villagers before they're slaughtered by the enemy troops. And if you encounter a mission with no timer you can bet that the opposition will be formidable, probably with a wave or two of reinfocements on top of what's already spawned on the map when you begin.
All in all this makes for an excellent game play that delivers a nerve wrecking experience even though the game is turn based.

This game alone is enough to make the year 2016 an awesome PC gaming year. What an amazing turn-based strategy game, with a staggering amount of nice character customization (especially with Steam Workshop mods). If you liked XCOM: Enemy Unknown, you will like this even more. If you never played the first one, you will still like this one. With a full mod support from the moment of release, and with the SDK now available, the game will have an extremely high replay value. We already have tons of great mod content, and its only getting better. Highly recommended to any and all friends of turn-based strategy games! If I believed in numeric ranking, this would be a solid 9/10.
Why not 10/10? My personal complaints:
- The game has some serious performance problems: with i7-3770k, 16GB RAM, GTX 970 and played from a 250GB Samsung EVO 850 SSD, @1440p or @1080p and medium/high settings (won't matter much), the game will average to about 35-50fps, will constantly drop below 25fps, sometimes even below 15fps(!). Lowering quality and/or resolution won't help much, so the problem is deep in the game. Holding steady 60fps is very rare.  This must be fixed ASAP! In its current condition, I'd say many gamers will lose their freakin' minds over this.
- late game content seems a bit unstable. I had 3 crashes during the last 4-5 hours of the game.
- EDIT: Stop Wasting My Time mod helps on this. "SHUT UP CENTRAL!" mod would be amazing! Im tired of that guy saying the same things over and over again, always cutting me off from my game. Why can't I just keep playing while that guy talks ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t? Stop cutting my game off!
- timed missions are partly great, but they have not been well developed here. A single mod made all the difference: mission timer start only when your team is revealed from concealment. This way you can play much more strategically, and without rushing like an idiot on some missions.

After playing for a time, I've come to the conclusion that this game isn't worth the time and effort.
Allow me to explain. The game is fun at first to goof around on, I'll give it that. The artwork is great, the feel is good, and it's got some good mechanics going for it. My issue is its replayability, and it has none. I understand with a dungeon game like this there really isn't much of an "end game" until muuuuch further down the line, but all you're doing in this game is replaying the same levels with the same enemies over and over and over again. There's no real progression, no point that you go "HELL YEAH! I'M GETTING SOMEWHERE!" and every game needs that. This is because the game rushes you through three tiers of gear and leveling and then goes "eh, fend for yourself" and you have to play the same stuff over and over again just to get the scraps to advance to the next level. There's no progression at this point, you get no sense of accomplishment from grinding the same levels for days because even if it's a slight challenge, it's the same thing every day.
What I'm really saying is that they need more variety. More enemies, more levels, more puzzles, more bosses, more more more. They need more so that the grind doesn't feel like a grind. Look at Runescape, a successful f2p mmo. Know why it's successful? The sheer amount of stuff to do when you want to grind.
In the end, I would say this game is a strong 5/10. Worth a moment if you're bored, but nothing to sink money and time into.

Don't waste your time, any fun this game had months prior to coming on steam was very methodically removed by the devs. The very over inflated cash shop prices help drive the point home that this will never become anything awesome either, just a vessel for cash scam.
The original concept of the game was a simplistic fun game that allowed large groups of people to collaborate into an army to eventually topple the mad god. People would band together in very large groups to help level each other and take down bosses. A fun concept but due to the simplistic nature of the game, hardly something you want to dole out money for, especially considering the game is built largely from graphics that are open source. Cash shop perks however created the rise of the "cashing loner" who could do alone what 50 or so players could accomplish. That also created these loners to corner anyone getting good equipment, creating a large rift in the player base, this essentially leads to 3 options in the game: 1) hack your way to the gear. 2) be forced to cash. 3) spend ages fighting for any progression.
Now these 3 routes are actually pretty typical of a free to play. Except Mad god has one more aspect that makes the taste even more sour, permadeath. Again with original concept of the game, permadeath wasn't so bad. The game was very pick up and play again, you didn't mind starting over because you never really had a lot of content to chew through so you never got too invested into any one character and there was other classes to try the game over from a new perspective. Now there is a lot more content to the game so dying for a free player even if they do as much planning as humanly possible, is a major setback, cash players can buy additional storage and even have soul bound items so they aren't exactly starting over every single time, adding to the gap between the players.
In all this game was a fun concept that was bled dry for every cent they could get and it shows plain as day.

I'm seeing a lot of reviews claiming hackers. I've played quite a few games by now and I have not seen any hackers.
I will explain what I do see. I see the effect of Ping/Latency and it manifests as times where you run behind a wall and you die to someone who seemed to have shot you through the wall. This is basically the effect of the local graphics rendering faster than the information from the server arrives to your PC to make your character actually die from getting shot.
Based on this latency issue, it could feel like people are hacking, but I haven't even seen K/D ratios reflect hackers in -any- of the games I have played. Some weapons are extremely powerful, such as the KSG shotgun, which allows you to essentially run around corners and simply click the instant you see someone, 1 shot = dead at close range. So it is possible to go on sprees and take out 5-6 guys in 5-6 shots if done properly. Mastering the aim and reflex time for that is part of the fun of these types of games, and there is no hacking involved, many times I go 30+ kills and 15-20 deaths, which is still positive K/D ratio.
All in all the game is decent, for a free to play you can get a few hours entertainment out of it and if you don't have any other first person shooters in the library then this one might be worth a try. Quick matches, and all in all pretty fun once you get the hang of it.

Good game, takes what XCOM did and expands upon the basic premise.
More enemies, more weapons, more maps, more gadgets, more classes, more customization, but essentially the same core gameplay.
Don't fix what isn't broken after all.
The two major complaints I've heard are difficulty and performance.
The difficulty is valid, this game is brutally difficult, and not really in a fun way. You're often thrown against simply unfair odds and a lot of missions have timers or objectives that kneecap any tactical approach you could have taken. Many of these situations break your immersion as you're supposed to be a resistance movement using guerilla tactics to strike at a larger, more powerful force, so many objectives just don't make a lot of sense. Often you'll be tasked with eliminating all enemy forces after completing an objective such as hacking a terminal and stealing data or stealing supplies from a train, when in reality a real guerilla force would just extract, the whole point is to AVOID engaging larger better equipped forces.
That said, don't be afraid to turn the difficulty down. I've found that the lowest difficulty is much closer to what I would have expected from "normal" in most games. I got my♥♥♥♥♥kicked in normal difficulty but easy is providing a fair challenge. Easy here is equivalent to normal in XCOM 1.
The performace is not valid.
This is a turn based game, it's not CSGO, the game isn't ruined if it dips below 60fps, dropped frames really don't matter if you're just watching an animation play out. Should it run a lot better than it does? Yes. Does sub-standard optimization make a turn based isometric strategy game unplayable? Of course not. I'm running it at medium settings and it's absolutely fine, it looks fine and runs fine. I don't expect every new AAA release to run in max settings on my mid range gaming PC and neither should you. People are blowing this out of proportion in an effort to manufacture outrage, but this isn't Arkham Knight, performance problems aren't going to ruin your experience here.
In summary turn down the difficulty and turn down your settings, then enjoy a very competent, however predictable, sequel.
